title.zh: 卷八十九 列傳第三十九: 狄仁傑 王方慶 姚璹
title.en: Volume 89 Biographies 39: Di Renjie, Wang Fangqing, Yao Shu
title.raw: 卷八十九 列傳第三十九: 狄仁傑 王方慶 姚璹 Volume 89 Biographies 39: Di Renjie, Wang Fangqing, Yao Shu

sentences.zh: 狄仁傑

translations.literal: Di Renjie
translations.idiomatic: Di Renjie

sentences.zh: （族曾孫兼謨）

translations.literal: (His clansman and great-grandson was Jian Mo.)
translations.idiomatic: (His clansman and great-grandson was Jian Mo.)

sentences.zh: 王方慶姚璹

translations.literal: Wang Fangqing and Yao Shu
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fangqing and Yao Shu

sentences.zh: （弟班）

translations.literal: (His younger brother was Ban.)
translations.idiomatic: (His younger brother was Ban.)

sentences.zh: 狄仁傑字懷英，并州太原人也。

translations.literal: Di Renjie, style name Huaiying, was a native of Taiyuan in Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Di Renjie, courtesy name Huaiying, was a native of Taiyuan in Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖孝緒，貞觀中尚書左丞。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xiao Xu was Left Vice Director of the Secretariat in the Zhenguan era.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xiao Xu served as Left Vice Director of the Secretariat during the Zhenguan reign.

sentences.zh: 父知遜，夔州長史。

translations.literal: His father Zhi Sun was long secretary of Kuizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhi Sun was chief secretary of Kuizhou.

sentences.zh: 仁傑兒童時，門人有被害者，縣吏就詰之，眾皆接對，唯仁傑堅坐讀書。

translations.literal: When Renjie was a child, one of his teachers was murdered, and the county clerk came to question them; everyone answered the questioning, but Renjie alone sat steadfastly reading.
translations.idiomatic: When Renjie was still a boy, one of his teachers was murdered. The county clerk came to question the pupils; everyone answered, but Renjie alone kept his seat and went on reading.

sentences.zh: 吏責之，仁傑曰：“黃卷之中，聖賢備在，猶不能接對，何暇偶俗吏，而見責耶！”

translations.literal: The clerk reproached him. Renjie said: "Within the yellow scrolls the sages and worthies are all present—if I cannot even answer to them, how could I spare time to meet vulgar clerks and be reproached by them!"
translations.idiomatic: The clerk scolded him. Renjie said, "The sages and worthies are all there in my books—if I cannot even answer to them, what leisure have I to bandy words with a petty clerk and take his rebuke!"

sentences.zh: 後以明經舉，授汴州判佐。

translations.literal: Later he was nominated through the Mingjing examination and was appointed assistant adjutant of Bianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later he passed the Mingjing examination and was appointed assistant adjutant of Bianzhou.

sentences.zh: 時工部尚書閻立本為河南道黜陟使，仁傑為吏人誣告，立本見而謝曰：“仲尼云：‘觀過知仁矣。

translations.literal: At the time Minister of Works Yan Liben was the Henan Circuit merit examiner. Renjie was falsely denounced by a clerk. When Liben met him he apologized and said: "Confucius said: 'Observe his errors and you know his benevolence.'"
translations.idiomatic: At the time Yan Liben, Minister of Works, was touring Henan as merit examiner. Renjie had been falsely denounced by a clerk. When Liben met him he apologized and said, "Confucius said, 'Observe a man's faults and you know his benevolence.'"

sentences.zh: ’足下可謂海曲之明珠，東南之遺寶。”

translations.literal: 'You may be called a bright pearl of the sea's bend, a treasure left behind in the southeast.'
translations.idiomatic: "You are a bright pearl from the sea's edge, a treasure the southeast has not yet lost."

sentences.zh: 薦授并州都督府法曹。

translations.literal: He recommended him and had him appointed legal clerk of the Bingzhou Protectorate Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended him and had him appointed legal clerk of the Bingzhou Protectorate.

sentences.zh: 其親在河陽別業，仁傑赴并州，登太行山，南望見白雲孤飛，謂左右曰：“吾親所居，在此雲下。”

translations.literal: His parents lived at a separate estate in Heyang. Renjie was traveling to Bingzhou and climbed Mount Taihang. Looking south he saw a lone cloud drifting and said to those beside him: "My parents dwell beneath this cloud."
translations.idiomatic: His parents lived at a separate estate in Heyang. On his way to Bingzhou Renjie climbed Mount Taihang; looking south he saw a lone cloud drifting and said to those beside him, "My parents live beneath that cloud."

sentences.zh: 瞻望佇立久之，雲移乃行。

translations.literal: He gazed and stood waiting a long time; only when the cloud moved did he proceed.
translations.idiomatic: He gazed after it and stood a long while; only when the cloud had moved on did he continue.

sentences.zh: 仁傑孝友絕人，在并州，有同府法曹鄭崇質，母老且病，當充使絕域。

translations.literal: Renjie's filial piety and brotherly affection surpassed all others. While in Bingzhou, there was a fellow legal clerk in the same office, Zheng Chongzhi, whose mother was old and ill and who was to serve as envoy to a distant region.
translations.idiomatic: Renjie's filial devotion and brotherly affection were unmatched. While he was in Bingzhou, a fellow legal clerk named Zheng Chongzhi had an aged, ailing mother and was assigned to serve as envoy to a distant land.

sentences.zh: 仁傑謂曰：“太夫人有危疾，而公遠使，豈可貽親萬里之憂！”

translations.literal: Renjie said to him: "Your venerable mother has a grave illness, yet you are to go on a distant mission—how could you leave your parent with worry a thousand miles away!"
translations.idiomatic: Renjie said to him, "Your mother is gravely ill, yet you are sent on a mission far away—how can you leave her with a thousand leagues of worry!"

sentences.zh: 乃詣長史藺仁基，請代崇質而行。

translations.literal: He then went to Chief Administrator Lin Renji and asked to go in Chongzhi's place.
translations.idiomatic: He then went to Chief Administrator Lin Renji and asked to go in Chongzhi's stead.

sentences.zh: 時仁基與司馬李孝廉不協，因謂曰：“吾等豈獨無愧耶？”

translations.literal: At the time Renji and Vice Commander Li Xiaolian were not on good terms. Because of this he said to him: "Are we alone without shame?"
translations.idiomatic: At the time Renji and Vice Commander Li Xiaolian were estranged. Because of this Renji said to Li, "Are we alone without shame?"

sentences.zh: 由是相待如初。

translations.literal: From this they treated each other as before.
translations.idiomatic: From that day they treated each other as before.

sentences.zh: 仁傑，儀鳳中為大理丞，周歲斷滯獄一萬七千人，無冤訴者。

translations.literal: During the Yifeng era Renjie served as assistant director of the Court of Judicial Review. Within a year he cleared backlogged cases involving seventeen thousand people, with none complaining of injustice.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yifeng era Renjie served as assistant director of the Court of Judicial Review. Within a year he cleared seventeen thousand backlogged cases, and no one complained of injustice.

sentences.zh: 時武衛大將軍權善才坐誤斫昭陵柏樹，仁傑奏罪當免職。

translations.literal: At the time Martial Guards General Quan Shancai was condemned for mistakenly cutting a cypress at Zhaoling. Renjie memorialized that the offence warranted dismissal from office.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Martial Guards General Quan Shancai was charged with mistakenly felling a cypress at Zhaoling. Renjie memorialized that the offence warranted only dismissal from office.

sentences.zh: 高宗令即誅之，仁傑又奏罪不當死。

translations.literal: Gaozong ordered him executed immediately. Renjie again memorialized that the crime did not warrant death.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong ordered him executed at once. Renjie again memorialized that the crime did not warrant death.

sentences.zh: 帝作色曰：“善才斫陵上樹，是使我不孝，必須殺之。”

translations.literal: The Emperor's face darkened and he said: "Shancai cut a tree on the imperial tomb—this makes me unfilial. He must be killed."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor's face darkened. "Shancai cut a tree on my father's tomb," he said. "That makes me unfilial. He must die."

sentences.zh: 左右矚仁傑令出，仁傑曰：“臣聞逆龍鱗，忤人主，自古以為難，臣愚以為不然。

translations.literal: Those at his side signaled Renjie to withdraw. Renjie said: "I have heard that opposing the dragon's scales and going against one's sovereign has since antiquity been considered difficult—but I, in my foolishness, do not think it so.
translations.idiomatic: Those at the Emperor's side signaled Renjie to withdraw. Renjie said, "I have heard that to touch the dragon's scales and oppose one's sovereign has always been called hard—but I, in my foolishness, do not think so.

sentences.zh: 居桀、紂時則難，堯、舜時則易。

translations.literal: Under Jie and Zhou it would be hard; under Yao and Shun it would be easy.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jie and Zhou it would be hard; under Yao and Shun it would be easy.

sentences.zh: 臣今幸逢堯、舜，不懼比幹之誅。

translations.literal: I now fortunately meet Yao and Shun, and do not fear the execution suffered by Bi Gan.
translations.idiomatic: I now have the good fortune to meet Yao and Shun, and do not fear the execution Bi Gan suffered.

sentences.zh: 昔漢文時有盜高廟玉環，張釋之廷諍，罪止棄市。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Wen of Han someone stole the jade ring from the Gaozu temple, and Zhang Shizhi remonstrated in court—the penalty was only public execution.
translations.idiomatic: In the reign of Emperor Wen of Han a man stole the jade ring from the Gaozu temple; Zhang Shizhi remonstrated in open court, and the penalty was only public execution.

sentences.zh: 魏文將徙其人，辛毗引裾而諫，亦見納用。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Wei was about to relocate his people, Xin Pi held his robe and remonstrated, and that too was accepted.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Wei was about to relocate his people, Xin Pi seized his robe and remonstrated, and that counsel too was accepted.

sentences.zh: 且明主可以理奪，忠臣不可以威懼。

translations.literal: Moreover, a wise sovereign may be persuaded by reason, but a loyal minister cannot be cowed by threats.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, a wise sovereign may be persuaded by reason, but a loyal minister must not be cowed by intimidation.

sentences.zh: 今陛下不納臣言，瞑目之後，羞見釋之、辛毗於地下。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty now does not accept my words, after I close my eyes I shall be ashamed to meet Shizhi and Xin Pi beneath the earth.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty will not heed me now, after I close my eyes I shall be ashamed to face Shizhi and Xin Pi in the grave.

sentences.zh: 陛下作法，懸之象魏，徒流死罪，俱有等差。

translations.literal: Your Majesty establishes law and hangs it at the gate-tower; exile, penal servitude, and capital punishment all have fixed gradations.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has established the law and hung it at the gate-tower; exile, penal servitude, and capital punishment each have their proper grades.

sentences.zh: 豈有犯非極刑，即令賜死？

translations.literal: How can there be an offence that is not capital punishment yet at once bring an order to bestow death?
translations.idiomatic: How can an offence that is not capital punishment at once be met with an order to bestow death?

sentences.zh: 法既無常，則萬姓何所措其手足？

translations.literal: If the law is without constancy, where shall the myriad people place their hands and feet?
translations.idiomatic: If the law has no fixed measure, where shall the common people place their hands and feet?

sentences.zh: 陛下必欲變法，請從今日為始。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty truly wishes to change the law, please let it begin from today.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty truly wishes to change the law, let it begin from today.

sentences.zh: 古人云：‘假使盜長陵一抔土，陛下何以加之？

translations.literal: The ancients said: 'Suppose someone stole a handful of earth from the Changling tomb—how would Your Majesty punish him?'
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said, 'Suppose a man stole a handful of earth from the Changling tomb—how would Your Majesty punish him?'

sentences.zh: ’今陛下以昭陵一株柏殺一將軍，千載之後，謂陛下為何主？

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty would kill a general for one cypress at Zhaoling—in a thousand years, what sort of ruler will people call Your Majesty?
translations.idiomatic: Yet now Your Majesty would kill a general for one cypress at Zhaoling—in a thousand years, what sort of ruler will men call you?

sentences.zh: 此臣所以不敢奉制殺善才，陷陛下於不道。”

translations.literal: This is why I dare not obey an order to kill Shancai and entangle Your Majesty in wrongdoing.
translations.idiomatic: That is why I dare not obey an order to kill Shancai and drag Your Majesty into wrongdoing.

sentences.zh: 帝意稍解，善才因而免死。

translations.literal: The Emperor's mood eased somewhat, and Shancai was spared death.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor's anger eased somewhat, and Shancai was spared.

sentences.zh: 居數日，授仁傑侍御史。

translations.literal: A few days later Renjie was appointed investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later Renjie was appointed investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 時司農卿韋機兼領將作、少府二司，高宗以恭陵玄宮狹小，不容送終之具，遣機續成其功。

translations.literal: At the time Minister of Public Works Wei Ji concurrently held the posts of Director of Palace Construction and Vice Minister of the Palace Department. Because Gaozong found the underground chamber of Gongling too narrow to hold the funeral furnishings, he sent Ji to continue and complete the work.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Minister of Public Works Wei Ji also held the posts of Director of Palace Construction and Vice Minister of the Palace Department. Because Emperor Gaozong found the underground chamber of Gongling too narrow for the funeral furnishings, he sent Ji to enlarge and complete it.

sentences.zh: 機於埏之左右為便房四所，又造宿羽、高山、上陽等宮，莫不壯麗。

translations.literal: Ji built four convenient chambers on either side of the platform, and also built the Su Yu, Gaoshan, and Shangyang palaces, all magnificent.
translations.idiomatic: Ji built four side chambers on either side of the platform, and also constructed the Su Yu, Gaoshan, and Shangyang palaces—none of them less than splendid.

sentences.zh: 仁傑奏其太過，機竟坐免官。

translations.literal: Renjie memorialized that this was excessive; Ji was ultimately dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Renjie memorialized that this was excessive, and Ji was ultimately dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 左司郎中王本立恃寵用事，朝廷懾懼，仁傑奏之，請付法寺，高宗特原之。

translations.literal: Left Department Director Wang Benli relied on favor to wield power; the court was in fear. Renjie memorialized against him and asked that he be handed to the judicial office. Gaozong specially pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Left Department Director Wang Benli relied on imperial favor to wield power, and the court trembled before him. Renjie memorialized against him and asked that he be handed over to the judicial office, but Emperor Gaozong specially pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 仁傑奏曰：“國家雖乏英才，豈少本立之類，陛下何惜罪人而虧王法？

translations.literal: Renjie memorialized: "Though the state may lack outstanding talent, are men like Benli so few? Why should Your Majesty spare a criminal and impair the royal law?"
translations.idiomatic: Renjie memorialized, "Though the state may lack outstanding talent, are men like Benli so scarce? Why should Your Majesty spare a criminal and impair the royal law?"

sentences.zh: 必欲曲赦本立，請棄臣於無人之境，為忠貞將來之誡。”

translations.literal: "If Your Majesty insists on bending the law to pardon Benli, please cast me out to a place where no man dwells, as a warning to the loyal and steadfast to come."
translations.idiomatic: "If Your Majesty insists on bending the law to pardon Benli, then cast me out to a place where no man dwells, as a warning to loyal ministers yet to come."

sentences.zh: 本立竟得罪，由是朝廷肅然。

translations.literal: Benli was ultimately punished; from this the court became orderly.
translations.idiomatic: Benli was ultimately punished, and from that day the court became orderly.

sentences.zh: 尋加朝散大夫，累遷度支郎中。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Palace Gentlemen Consultant and successively advanced to Director of the Revenue Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to Palace Gentlemen Consultant and then successively to Director of the Revenue Bureau.

sentences.zh: 高宗將幸汾陽宮，以仁傑為知頓使。

translations.literal: When Gaozong was about to visit the Fenyang Palace, Renjie was made provisioning commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong was about to visit the Fenyang Palace, Renjie was appointed provisioning commissioner.

sentences.zh: 并州長史李衝玄以道出妒女祠，俗雲盛服過者必致風雷之災，乃發數萬人別開御道。

translations.literal: Bingzhou Chief Administrator Li Chongxuan, because the route passed the Jealous Woman Shrine—it was said that anyone passing in grand attire would bring wind and thunder—mobilized tens of thousands of men to open a separate imperial road.
translations.idiomatic: Bingzhou Chief Administrator Li Chongxuan, because the route passed the Jealous Woman Shrine—it was said that anyone passing in grand attire would bring wind and thunder—mobilized tens of thousands of men to cut a separate imperial road.

sentences.zh: 仁傑曰：“天子之行，千乘萬騎，風伯清塵，雨師灑道，何妒女之害耶？”

translations.literal: Renjie said: "When the Son of Heaven travels, a thousand chariots and ten thousand riders go forth—the Wind Lord clears the dust and the Rain Master sprinkles the road. What harm could the Jealous Woman do?"
translations.idiomatic: Renjie said, "When the Son of Heaven travels, a thousand chariots and ten thousand riders go forth—the Wind Lord clears the dust and the Rain Master sprinkles the road. What harm could the Jealous Woman do?"

sentences.zh: 遽令罷之。

translations.literal: He immediately ordered it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately ordered the work stopped.

sentences.zh: 高宗聞之，歎曰：“真大丈夫也！”

translations.literal: When Gaozong heard of it he sighed: "A true great man!"
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong heard of it he sighed, "A true great man!"

sentences.zh: 俄轉寧州刺史，撫和戎夏，人得歡心，郡人勒碑頌德。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Prefect of Ningzhou, where he soothed both Chinese and barbarians; the people were won over, and the people of the commandery carved a stele praising his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to Prefect of Ningzhou, where he soothed both Chinese and barbarians alike. The people were won to him, and the people of the commandery carved a stele praising his virtue.

sentences.zh: 御史郭翰巡察隴右，所至多所按劾。

translations.literal: Censor Guo Han inspected Longyou; wherever he went he prosecuted many cases.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Guo Han inspected Longyou; wherever he went he prosecuted many cases.

sentences.zh: 及入寧州境內，耆老歌刺史德美者盈路。

translations.literal: When he entered Ningzhou's territory, the elders singing of the prefect's virtue filled the road.
translations.idiomatic: When he entered Ningzhou's territory, elders singing the prefect's praises filled the road.

sentences.zh: 翰既授館，召州吏謂之曰：“ 入其境，其政可知也。

translations.literal: After Han had taken lodging, he summoned the prefectural clerks and said: "Entering a territory, its governance can be known.
translations.idiomatic: After Han had taken lodging, he summoned the prefectural clerks and said, "Enter a territory and its governance can be known.

sentences.zh: 願成使君之美，無為久留。”

translations.literal: I wish to complete the prefect's excellence—do not detain me long."
translations.idiomatic: I wish to complete the prefect's good name—do not keep me long."

sentences.zh: 州人方散。

translations.literal: The people of the prefecture then dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: The people of the prefecture then dispersed.

sentences.zh: 翰薦名於朝，徵為冬官侍郎，充江南巡撫使。

translations.literal: Han recommended his name to the court; he was summoned as Vice Minister of the Ministry of Works and appointed commissioner touring Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Han recommended him to the court; he was summoned as Vice Minister of the Ministry of Works and appointed commissioner touring Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 吳、楚之俗多淫祠，仁傑奏毀一千七百所，唯留夏禹、吳太伯、季劄、伍員四祠。

translations.literal: Wu and Chu customs had many licentious shrines. Renjie memorialized to destroy seventeen hundred of them, retaining only the shrines to Yu the Great, Wu Taibo, Ji Zha, and Wu Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: In Wu and Chu the custom favored licentious shrines. Renjie memorialized to destroy seventeen hundred of them, retaining only the shrines to Yu the Great, Wu Taibo, Ji Zha, and Wu Yuan.

sentences.zh: 轉文昌右丞，出為豫州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Right Vice Director of the Secretariat and sent out as Prefect of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Right Vice Director of the Secretariat and sent out as Prefect of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 時越王貞稱兵汝南事敗，緣坐者六七百人，籍沒者五千口，司刑使逼促行刑。

translations.literal: At the time when Prince Yue raised troops at Runan and was defeated, those implicated numbered six or seven hundred, and five thousand persons had their households registered for confiscation. The judicial commissioner urgently pressed for executions.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Prince Yue of Yue had raised troops at Runan and been defeated; those implicated numbered six or seven hundred, and five thousand persons had their households registered for confiscation. The judicial commissioner pressed urgently for executions.

sentences.zh: 仁傑哀其詿誤，緩其獄，密表奏曰：“臣欲顯奏，似為逆人申理；

translations.literal: Renjie pitied those who had been ensnared in error, slowed the cases, and secretly memorialized: "If I openly report this, it will seem that I am arguing for the rebels;"
translations.idiomatic: Renjie pitied those ensnared in error, slowed the cases, and secretly memorialized, "If I report this openly, it will seem that I am pleading for rebels;"

sentences.zh: 知而不言，恐乖陛下存恤之旨。

translations.literal: "yet if I know and do not speak, I fear I would violate Your Majesty's intent to preserve and soothe."
translations.idiomatic: yet if I know and do not speak, I fear I would violate Your Majesty's intent to preserve and soothe."

sentences.zh: 表成復毀，意不能定。

translations.literal: "When the memorial was finished I destroyed it again—my mind could not be settled."
translations.idiomatic: "When the memorial was finished I destroyed it again—my mind could not be settled."

sentences.zh: 此輩鹹非本心，伏望哀其詿誤。”

translations.literal: "These people were none of them of their own hearts in this; I humbly hope you will pity those ensnared in error."
translations.idiomatic: "None of these people acted from their own hearts; I humbly beg pity for those ensnared in error."

sentences.zh: 特敕原之，配流豐州。

translations.literal: By special edict they were pardoned and assigned to exile in Fengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: By special edict they were pardoned and assigned to exile in Fengzhou.

sentences.zh: 豫囚次於寧州，父老迎而勞之曰：“我狄使君活汝輩耶！”

translations.literal: The Yuzhou prisoners, passing through Ningzhou, were welcomed and comforted by the elders who said: "Did our Prefect Di save you!"
translations.idiomatic: The Yuzhou prisoners, passing through Ningzhou, were welcomed by the elders, who said, "Did Prefect Di save you!"

sentences.zh: 相攜哭於碑下，齋三日而後行。

translations.literal: They wept together at the stele, fasted three days, and then departed.
translations.idiomatic: They wept together at the stele, fasted three days, and then went on.

sentences.zh: 豫囚至流所，復相與立碑頌狄君之德。

translations.literal: When the Yuzhou prisoners reached the place of exile, they again together erected a stele praising Prefect Di's virtue.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yuzhou prisoners reached their place of exile, they again together erected a stele praising Prefect Di's virtue.

sentences.zh: 初，越王之亂，宰相張光輔率師討平之。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the Prince of Yue's rebellion, Chancellor Zhang Guangfu led troops to suppress and pacify it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during the Prince of Yue's rebellion, Chancellor Zhang Guangfu had led troops to suppress and pacify it.

sentences.zh: 將士恃功，多所求取，仁傑不之應。

translations.literal: The officers and soldiers, relying on their merit, made many demands; Renjie did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: The officers and soldiers, relying on their merit, made many demands, but Renjie did not comply.

sentences.zh: 光輔怒曰：“州將輕元帥耶？”

translations.literal: Guangfu angrily said: "Does the prefect slight the commander-in-chief?"
translations.idiomatic: Guangfu said angrily, "Does the prefect slight the commander-in-chief?"

sentences.zh: 仁傑曰：“亂河南者，一越王貞耳。

translations.literal: Renjie said: "The one who disturbed Henan was only Prince Yue of Yue."
translations.idiomatic: Renjie said, "The one who disturbed Henan was only Prince Yue of Yue."

sentences.zh: 今一貞死而萬貞生。”

translations.literal: "Now one Yue is dead, but ten thousand Yues are born."
translations.idiomatic: "Now one Yue is dead, but ten thousand Yues are born."

sentences.zh: 光輔質其辭，仁傑曰：“明公董戎三十萬，平一亂臣，不戢兵鋒，縱其暴橫，無罪之人，肝腦塗地，此非萬貞何耶？

translations.literal: Guangfu challenged his words. Renjie said: "Your Excellency supervised an army of three hundred thousand and pacified one rebel—yet you did not sheathe your blades and let them run wild. Innocent people had their livers and brains smeared on the ground—is this not ten thousand Yues?"
translations.idiomatic: Guangfu challenged his words. Renjie said, "Your Excellency led three hundred thousand troops and pacified one rebel—yet you did not sheathe your blades and let them run wild. Innocent people had their livers and brains smeared on the ground—is this not ten thousand Yues?"

sentences.zh: 且凶威協從，勢難自固，及天兵暫臨，乘城歸順者萬計，繩墜四面成蹊。

translations.literal: "Moreover those who joined from coercion could hardly hold firm on their own; when the imperial army briefly arrived, those who climbed the walls and submitted numbered in the tens of thousands—ropes by which men climbed fell away on all four sides, making paths."
translations.idiomatic: "Moreover those who followed under coercion could hardly stand firm on their own; when the imperial army briefly arrived, those who climbed the walls and submitted numbered in the tens of thousands—ropes by which men climbed fell away on all four sides, making paths."

sentences.zh: 公奈何縱邀功之人，殺歸降之眾？

translations.literal: "Why do you indulgence those who claim merit and kill those who surrendered?"
translations.idiomatic: "Why do you indulge those who claim merit and kill those who surrendered?"

sentences.zh: 但恐冤聲騰沸，上徹於天。

translations.literal: "I only fear that cries of injustice will boil up and pierce heaven."
translations.idiomatic: "I only fear that cries of injustice will boil up and pierce heaven itself."

sentences.zh: 如得尚方斬馬劍加於君頸，雖死如歸。”

translations.literal: "If the emperor's sword of execution were placed upon your neck, I would meet death as gladly as going home."
translations.idiomatic: "If the emperor's sword of execution were placed upon your neck, I would meet death as gladly as going home."

sentences.zh: 光輔不能詰，心甚銜之。

translations.literal: Guangfu could not rebut him and deeply resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Guangfu could not rebut him and deeply resented him.

sentences.zh: 還都，奏仁傑不遜，左授復州刺史。

translations.literal: On returning to the capital he memorialized that Renjie was insubordinate; Renjie was demoted to Prefect of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to the capital he memorialized that Renjie was insubordinate, and Renjie was demoted to Prefect of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 入為洛州司馬。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Vice Magistrate of Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the capital as Vice Magistrate of Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 天授二年九月丁酉，轉地官侍郎、判尚書、同鳳閣鸞台平章事。

translations.literal: On the ninth month, day dingyou of the second year of Tianshou, he was transferred to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Revenue, concurrently Director of the Secretariat, and Associate at the Hall of the Phoenix and Hall of the Crane with equal authority as chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingyou day of the ninth month in the second year of Tianshou, he was transferred to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Revenue, concurrently Director of the Secretariat, and Associate at the Hall of the Phoenix and Hall of the Crane with the authority of a chancellor.

sentences.zh: 則天謂曰：“卿在汝南時，甚有善政，欲知譖卿者乎？”

translations.literal: Wu Zetian said to him: "When you were at Runan you had very good governance. Would you like to know who slandered you?"
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu said to him, "When you were at Runan your governance was excellent. Would you like to know who slandered you?"

sentences.zh: 仁傑謝曰：“陛下以臣為過，臣當改之；

translations.literal: Renjie replied: "If Your Majesty take me to have faults, I should reform them;"
translations.idiomatic: Renjie replied, "If Your Majesty deem me at fault, I shall reform;"

sentences.zh: 陛下明臣無過，臣之幸也。

translations.literal: "if Your Majesty know me to be without fault, that is my good fortune."
translations.idiomatic: if Your Majesty know me to be without fault, that is my good fortune."

sentences.zh: 臣不知譖者，並為善友，臣請不知。”

translations.literal: "I do not wish to know the slanderers—they would all become good friends; I ask not to know."
translations.idiomatic: "I do not wish to know the slanderers—they would all become good friends. I ask not to know."

sentences.zh: 則天深加歎異。

translations.literal: Wu Zetian deeply sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu sighed deeply in admiration.

sentences.zh: 未幾，為來俊臣誣構下獄。

translations.literal: Before long he was falsely implicated by Lai Junchen and thrown into prison.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was falsely implicated by Lai Junchen and thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 時一問即承者例得減死，來俊臣逼協仁傑，令一問承反。

translations.literal: At the time those who confessed at the first questioning were by precedent entitled to commuted death. Lai Junchen pressured Renjie and ordered him to confess to rebellion at the first questioning.
translations.idiomatic: At the time those who confessed at the first questioning were by precedent entitled to commuted death. Lai Junchen pressured Renjie and ordered him to confess to rebellion at the first questioning.

sentences.zh: 仁傑歎曰：“大周革命，萬物唯新，唐朝舊臣，甘從誅戮。

translations.literal: Renjie sighed: "The Great Zhou has undergone revolution; all things are renewed. I, an old minister of Tang, gladly accept execution."
translations.idiomatic: Renjie sighed, "The Great Zhou has undergone revolution and all things are renewed. I, an old minister of Tang, gladly accept execution."

sentences.zh: 反是實！”

translations.literal: "Rebellion is the truth!"
translations.idiomatic: "Rebellion is the truth!"

sentences.zh: 俊臣乃少寬之。

translations.literal: Junchen then eased up somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: Junchen then eased up somewhat.

sentences.zh: 判官王德壽謂仁傑曰：“尚書必得減死。

translations.literal: Judge Wang Deshou said to Renjie: "The Minister will certainly receive commuted death."
translations.idiomatic: Judge Wang Deshou said to Renjie, "The Minister will certainly receive commuted death."

sentences.zh: 德壽意欲求少階級，憑尚書牽楊執柔，可乎？”

translations.literal: "Deshou wishes to gain a small promotion—by relying on the Minister to implicate Yang Zhirou, would that be possible?"
translations.idiomatic: "Deshou wishes to gain a small promotion—by relying on the Minister to implicate Yang Zhirou, would that be possible?"

sentences.zh: 仁傑曰：“若何牽之？”

translations.literal: Renjie said: "How would I implicate him?"
translations.idiomatic: Renjie said, "How would I implicate him?"

sentences.zh: 德壽曰：“尚書為春官時，執柔任其司員外，引之可也。”

translations.literal: Deshou said: "When the Minister was in the Ministry of Personnel, Zhirou served as director of his section; he could be implicated."
translations.idiomatic: Deshou said, "When the Minister was in the Ministry of Personnel, Zhirou served as director of his section; he could be implicated."

sentences.zh: 仁傑曰：“皇天後土，遣仁傑行此事！”

translations.literal: Renjie said, "Heaven and Earth have dispatched Renjie to perform this deed!"
translations.idiomatic: Renjie cried out, "Heaven and Earth have sent me to do such a thing!"

sentences.zh: 以頭觸柱，流血被麵，德壽懼而謝焉。

translations.literal: He struck his head against a pillar; blood covered his face. Deshou was frightened and apologized.
translations.idiomatic: He dashed his head against a pillar until blood covered his face. Deshou was terrified and begged his forgiveness.

sentences.zh: 既承反，所司但待日行刑，不復嚴備。

translations.literal: Having already confessed to rebellion, the officials merely awaited the day of execution and no longer maintained strict guard.
translations.idiomatic: Once he had confessed to rebellion, the officials simply waited for execution day and relaxed their vigilance.

sentences.zh: 仁傑求守者得筆硯，拆被頭帛書冤，置綿衣中，謂德壽曰：“時方熱，請付家人去其綿。”

translations.literal: Renjie obtained brush and inkstone from a guard, tore fabric from the quilt cover to write of his innocence, placed it inside a padded garment, and said to Deshou, "It is hot just now; please give this to my family to remove the padding."
translations.idiomatic: Renjie got brush and ink from a guard, tore cloth from his quilt to write a plea of innocence, hid it in a padded coat, and told Deshou, "The weather is hot—please send this to my family so they can remove the cotton lining."

sentences.zh: 德壽不之察。

translations.literal: Deshou did not examine it.
translations.idiomatic: Deshou never looked into it.

sentences.zh: 仁傑子光遠得書，持以告變。

translations.literal: Renjie's son Guangyuan received the letter and took it to report the matter as an emergency.
translations.idiomatic: Renjie's son Guangyuan received the letter and rushed to report the affair to the throne.

sentences.zh: 則天召見，覽之而問俊臣。

translations.literal: Empress Wu summoned him for audience, read it, and questioned Jun Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu summoned Renjie, read the letter, and questioned Lai Jun Chen.

sentences.zh: 俊臣曰：“仁傑不免冠帶，寢處甚安，何由伏罪？”

translations.literal: Jun Chen said, "Renjie still wears cap and sash; his sleeping quarters are quite comfortable. How could he have confessed guilt?"
translations.idiomatic: Jun Chen said, "Renjie still goes about in full dress and sleeps in comfort. How could he possibly have admitted guilt?"

sentences.zh: 則天使人視之，俊臣遽命仁傑巾帶而見使者。

translations.literal: The Empress sent someone to inspect him, and Jun Chen immediately ordered Renjie to put on headcloth and sash before meeting the envoy.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress sent an inspector, and Jun Chen at once ordered Renjie to don cap and sash before the envoy arrived.

sentences.zh: 乃令德壽代仁傑作謝死表，附使者進之。

translations.literal: He then had Deshou write a memorial accepting death on Renjie's behalf and had it submitted through the envoy.
translations.idiomatic: He then had Deshou draft a memorial of thanks for execution in Renjie's name and sent it in with the envoy.

sentences.zh: 則天召仁傑，謂曰：“承反何也？”

translations.literal: Empress Wu summoned Renjie and said, "Why did you confess to rebellion?"
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu summoned Renjie and asked, "Why did you confess to rebellion?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：“向若不承反，已死於鞭笞矣。”

translations.literal: He replied, "If I had not confessed to rebellion earlier, I would already have died under the lash."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "If I had not confessed to rebellion, I would already have been beaten to death."

sentences.zh: “何為作謝死表？”

translations.literal: Why did you write a memorial accepting death?"
translations.idiomatic: Then why was a memorial accepting death written?"

sentences.zh: 曰“臣無此表。”

translations.literal: He said, "Your subject has no such memorial."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "I wrote no such memorial."

sentences.zh: 示之，乃知代署也。

translations.literal: When it was shown to him, he then knew it had been written in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: When she showed it to him, he realized it had been forged in his name.

sentences.zh: 故得免死。

translations.literal: Thus he was spared death.
translations.idiomatic: In this way he was spared execution.

sentences.zh: 貶彭澤令。

translations.literal: He was demoted to magistrate of Pengze.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to magistrate of Pengze County.

sentences.zh: 武承嗣屢奏請誅之，則天曰：“朕好生惡殺，誌在恤刑。

translations.literal: Wu Chengsi repeatedly memorialized requesting his execution. Empress Wu said, "I love life and hate killing; my intent is to show mercy in punishment."
translations.idiomatic: Wu Chengsi repeatedly petitioned for his execution, but Empress Wu said, "I cherish life and abhor killing; my purpose is to temper justice with mercy."

sentences.zh: 渙汗已行，不可更返。”

translations.literal: The decree of grace has already been issued and cannot be reversed.
translations.idiomatic: A pardon has already been granted and cannot be withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 萬歲通天年，契丹寇陷冀州，河北震動，征仁傑為魏州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Wansui Tongtian era, the Khitan raided and captured Jizhou; Hebei was shaken, and Renjie was summoned to serve as prefect of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wansui Tongtian era, Khitan invaders captured Jizhou and threw Hebei into turmoil; Renjie was appointed prefect of Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 前刺史獨孤思莊懼賊至，盡驅百姓入城，繕修守具。

translations.literal: The previous prefect, Dugu Sizhuang, fearing the arrival of bandits, drove all the common people into the city and repaired the defensive equipment.
translations.idiomatic: The previous prefect, Dugu Sizhuang, fearing an attack, herded all the people into the city and set about repairing the defenses.

sentences.zh: 仁傑既至，悉放歸農畝，謂曰：“賊猶在遠，何必如是。

translations.literal: When Renjie arrived, he released them all to return to their fields and said, "The bandits are still far away—why act like this?"
translations.idiomatic: When Renjie arrived, he sent them all back to their farms and said, "The enemy is still far off—there is no need for this."

sentences.zh: 萬一賊來，吾自當之，必不關百姓也。”

translations.literal: If by chance the bandits come, I myself will meet them; it will certainly not involve the common people.
translations.idiomatic: If the enemy should come, I will face them myself and will not involve the common people.

sentences.zh: 賊聞之自退，百姓鹹歌誦之，相與立碑以紀恩惠。

translations.literal: When the bandits heard of this they withdrew of themselves; the people all sang and recited praises of him, and together they erected a stele to record his kindness.
translations.idiomatic: When the raiders heard this they withdrew on their own; the people sang his praises everywhere, and together they erected a stele to commemorate his benevolence.

sentences.zh: 俄轉幽州都督。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was transferred to regional inspector of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to regional inspector of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 神功元年，入為鸞台侍郎、同鳳閣鸞台平章事，加銀青光祿大夫，兼納言。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Shen Gong era, he entered the court as vice minister of the Luantai, associate director of the Fengge-Luantai Secretariat, was promoted to Silver Blue-Gleaming Glory Grand Master, and concurrently served as director of memorials.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Shen Gong era, he entered court as vice minister of the Luantai and associate chief minister of the Fengge-Luantai Secretariat, was granted the title Silver Blue-Gleaming Glory Grand Master, and concurrently served as director of memorials.

sentences.zh: 仁傑以百姓西戍疏勒等四鎮，極為凋弊，乃上疏曰：

translations.literal: Renjie, because the common people garrisoning the four western posts such as Kashgar were extremely exhausted and impoverished, submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Renjie, seeing how severely the people were depleted by garrison duty in the four western posts including Kashgar, submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 臣聞天生四夷，皆在先王封疆之外。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that Heaven gave birth to the four barbarian peoples, all of them lying beyond the frontiers of the former kings.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that Heaven created the four barbarian peoples, and that all of them lay beyond the domains of the ancient kings.

sentences.zh: 故東拒滄海，西隔流沙，北橫大漠，南阻五嶺，此天所以限夷狄而隔中外也。

translations.literal: Therefore the east was blocked by the Blue Sea, the west separated by flowing sands, the north crossed by the great desert, and the south obstructed by the Five Ridges—this is how Heaven limited the barbarians and divided the inner from the outer realms.
translations.idiomatic: The east was bounded by the sea, the west by shifting sands, the north by the great desert, and the south by the Five Ridges—this was Heaven's way of confining the barbarians and separating the civilized center from the outer world.

sentences.zh: 自典籍所紀，聲教所及，三代不能至者，國家盡兼之矣。

translations.literal: From what the classics record and where civilization reached, what the Three Dynasties could not attain, our state has fully annexed.
translations.idiomatic: Of all the lands recorded in the classics and reached by civilization, those the Three Dynasties never controlled, our state now holds in full.

sentences.zh: 此則今日之四境，已逾於夏、殷者也。

translations.literal: Thus the four borders of today already exceed those of Xia and Yin.
translations.idiomatic: The realm's four borders today already surpass those of the Xia and Yin dynasties.

sentences.zh: 詩人矜薄伐於太原，美化行於江、漢，則是前代之遠裔，而國家之域中。

translations.literal: The poets praised a restrained campaign at Taiyuan, and civilization extended to the Yangtze and Han—what were distant frontiers in former ages are now within our state's domain.
translations.idiomatic: Poets once praised a limited campaign at Taiyuan, and civilization reached the Yangtze and Han—lands that were remote frontiers in earlier ages are now well within the heartland of the state.

sentences.zh: 至前漢時，匈奴無歲不陷邊，殺掠吏人。

translations.literal: By the time of Former Han, the Xiongnu raided the borders every year without fail, killing and plundering officials and people.
translations.idiomatic: By the Former Han, the Xiongnu breached the frontier every single year, killing officials and plundering the people.

sentences.zh: 後漢則西羌侵軼漢中，東寇三輔，入河東上黨，幾至洛陽。

translations.literal: In Later Han the Western Qiang raided Hanzhong, attacked the Three Metropolises in the east, entered Hedong and Shangdang, and nearly reached Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In Later Han the Western Qiang overran Hanzhong, raided the Three Metropolises in the east, penetrated Hedong and Shangdang, and almost reached Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 由此言之，則陛下今日之士宇，過於漢朝遠矣。

translations.literal: Spoken from this perspective, Your Majesty's territory today far surpasses that of the Han dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: From this it follows that Your Majesty's domain today far exceeds that of the Han.

sentences.zh: 若其用武荒外，邀功絕域，竭府庫之實，以爭磽確不毛之地，得其人不足以增賦，獲其土不可以耕織。

translations.literal: If one uses force in the wilderness beyond, seeks merit in distant regions, and exhausts the treasury's substance to fight for barren, infertile land, the people gained would not suffice to increase taxes, and the soil taken could not be farmed or woven upon.
translations.idiomatic: If we use force in distant wastes, seek glory in far-off lands, and drain the treasury to seize barren ground, the people we gain would not increase revenue, and the soil we take cannot be farmed or woven.

sentences.zh: 苟求冠帶遠夷之稱，不務固本安人之術，此秦皇、漢武之所行，非五帝、三皇之事業也。

translations.literal: If one merely seeks the reputation of bringing distant barbarians into cap and sash, and does not devote oneself to methods of strengthening the foundation and securing the people, this is what the First Emperor of Qin and Emperor Wu of Han did—not the achievement of the Five Emperors and Three Sage-Kings.
translations.idiomatic: If we merely chase the empty honor of civilizing distant barbarians instead of strengthening the foundation and securing the people, we follow the path of the First Emperor of Qin and Emperor Wu of Han—not the way of the Five Emperors and Three Sage-Kings.

sentences.zh: 若使越荒外以為限，竭資財以騁欲，非但不愛人力，亦所以失天心也。

translations.literal: If one crosses the wilderness to set boundaries and exhausts resources to indulge desire, this not only fails to cherish human labor but also forfeits Heaven's favor.
translations.idiomatic: To push beyond the wilderness in pursuit of borders and exhaust the state's wealth to satisfy ambition is not only to squander human labor but also to lose Heaven's favor.

sentences.zh: 昔始皇窮兵極武，以求廣地，男子不得耕於野，女子不得蠶於室，長城之下，死者如亂麻，於是天下潰叛。

translations.literal: Formerly the First Emperor exhausted military force to the utmost in seeking broad territory; men could not plow in the fields, women could not raise silkworms at home, and beneath the Great Wall the dead lay tangled like hemp—whereupon the realm collapsed in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In the past the First Emperor exhausted every resource for war to expand his domain; men could not farm in the fields, women could not raise silkworms at home, and beneath the Great Wall the dead lay in heaps like tangled hemp—until the realm collapsed in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 漢武追高、文之宿憤，藉四帝之儲實，於是定朝鮮，討西域，平南越，擊匈奴，府庫空虛，盜賊蜂起，百姓嫁妻賣子，流離於道路者萬計。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Han pursued the longstanding resentment of Emperors Gao and Wen, relying on the accumulated reserves of four emperors; thereupon he settled Korea, campaigned in the Western Regions, pacified Southern Yue, and struck the Xiongnu. The treasury was emptied, bandits swarmed like bees, the people sold wives and children, and those wandering destitute on the roads numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Han, pursuing the old humiliations borne by Emperors Gao and Wen and drawing on the accumulated wealth of four reigns, then settled Korea, campaigned in the Western Regions, pacified Southern Yue, and attacked the Xiongnu. The treasury was emptied, bandits rose everywhere, people sold wives and children, and tens of thousands wandered destitute along the roads.

sentences.zh: 末年覺悟，息兵罷役，封丞相為富民侯，故能為天所祐也。

translations.literal: In his later years he awakened, ceased warfare and halted corvée labor, and enfeoffed the chancellor as Marquis of Enriching the People; thus he could be protected by Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In his final years he came to his senses, halted warfare and labor conscription, and enfeoffed his chancellor as Marquis of Enriching the People—thus he regained Heaven's protection.

sentences.zh: 昔人有言：“與覆車同軌者未嚐安。”

translations.literal: Someone in former times said, "Those who follow the tracks of an overturned cart have never been safe."
translations.idiomatic: As someone once said, "Those who follow the ruts of an overturned cart have never come to safety."

sentences.zh: 此言雖小，可以喻大。

translations.literal: Though this saying is small, it can illustrate a great matter.
translations.idiomatic: Though the saying is modest, it speaks to a great truth.

sentences.zh: 近者國家頻歲出師，所費滋廣，西戍四鎮，東戍安東，調發日加，百姓虛弊。

translations.literal: Recently the state has sent out armies year after year; expenses grow ever greater. Garrisons stand in the four western posts and in Andong in the east; levies increase daily, and the common people are depleted and exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years the state has launched campaigns year after year at ever greater cost. We garrison the four western posts and Andong in the east; levies increase daily while the people grow hollow and exhausted.

sentences.zh: 開守西域，事等石田，費用不支，有損無益，轉輸靡絕，杼軸殆空。

translations.literal: Opening and garrisoning the Western Regions is like farming stone fields: expenses cannot be sustained, there is harm without benefit, transport never ceases, and the looms are nearly empty.
translations.idiomatic: Holding the Western Regions is like trying to farm stone fields—costs cannot be sustained, the harm outweighs any gain, supply lines never stop, and the looms stand nearly idle.

sentences.zh: 越磧逾海，分兵防守，行役既久，怨曠亦多。

translations.literal: Crossing deserts and seas, dividing troops to garrison and defend, service has already been long, and resentment and loneliness are also abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Crossing deserts and seas to post troops on distant guard duty, the service stretches on and on, and resentment and loneliness mount.

sentences.zh: 昔詩人云：“王事靡盬，不能藝稷黍。”

translations.literal: The poets of old said, "The king's affairs never cease; we cannot plant millet and glutinous millet."
translations.idiomatic: The poets of old wrote, "The king's service never ends; we cannot plant our millet and grain."

sentences.zh: “ 豈不懷歸，畏此罪罟。

translations.literal: Do we not long to return home? We fear this punishment and snare."
translations.idiomatic: Do we not yearn to go home? We fear this punishment and snare."

sentences.zh: 念彼蒸人，涕零如雨。”

translations.literal: Thinking of those people, tears fall like rain.
translations.idiomatic: Thinking of those people, tears fall like rain.

sentences.zh: 此則前代怨思之辭也。

translations.literal: These are words of resentment and longing from former ages.
translations.idiomatic: These are the words of resentment and longing from ages past.

sentences.zh: 上不是恤，則政不行而邪氣作；

translations.literal: If the ruler above does not show concern, then government will not be carried out and perverse qi will arise;
translations.idiomatic: When the ruler above shows no concern, government fails and perverse forces arise;

sentences.zh: 邪氣作，則蟲螟生而水旱起。

translations.literal: when perverse qi arises, then locusts and caterpillars are born and floods and droughts occur.
translations.idiomatic: when perverse forces arise, locusts swarm and floods and droughts follow.

sentences.zh: 若此，雖禱祀百神，不能調陰陽矣。

translations.literal: If matters are like this, even though one prays and sacrifices to the hundred gods, one cannot harmonize yin and yang.
translations.idiomatic: When things reach this point, even prayers and sacrifices to every god cannot restore harmony between yin and yang.

sentences.zh: 方今關東饑饉，蜀、漢逃亡，江、淮以南，徵求不息。

translations.literal: At present there is famine east of the Pass; in Shu and Han people flee; south of the Yangtze and Huai, exactions never cease.
translations.idiomatic: Right now famine grips the lands east of the Pass, people flee from Shu and Han, and south of the Yangtze and Huai exactions never stop.

sentences.zh: 人不復業，則相率為盜，本根一搖，憂患不淺。

translations.literal: If people cannot resume their livelihoods, then they will successively become bandits; once the foundation is shaken, the troubles will not be slight.
translations.idiomatic: When people cannot return to their livelihoods, they turn to banditry in droves; once the foundation is shaken, the troubles will be grave indeed.

sentences.zh: 其所以然者，皆為遠戍方外，以竭中國，爭蠻貊不毛之地，乖子養蒼生之道也。

translations.literal: The reasons for this are all that distant garrisoning beyond the borders exhausts the Central Land, fighting for barbarian, infertile soil, and departs from the Way of nurturing the living masses.
translations.idiomatic: The root cause is garrisoning distant frontiers at the cost of exhausting the heartland, fighting over barbarian wastes, and abandoning the duty to nurture the people.

sentences.zh: 昔漢元納賈捐之之謀而罷珠崖郡，宣帝用魏相之策而棄車師之田，豈不欲慕尚虛名，蓋憚勞人力也。

translations.literal: Formerly Emperor Yuan of Han accepted Jia Juanzhi's plan and abolished Zhuya Commandery; Emperor Xuan used Wei Xiang's strategy and abandoned the fields of Jushi. Was this not because they did not desire empty glory, but feared to burden human labor?
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Emperor Yuan of Han accepted Jia Juanzhi's counsel and abolished Zhuya Commandery, and Emperor Xuan adopted Wei Xiang's plan and abandoned the fields of Jushi—not because they lacked ambition for glory, but because they feared to overtax the people.

sentences.zh: 近貞觀年中，克平九姓，冊李思摩為可汗，使統諸部者，蓋以夷狄叛則伐之，降則撫之，得推亡固存之義，無遠戍勞人之役。

translations.literal: Recently in the Zhenguan era, after conquering the Nine Surnames, Li Simo was invested as khagan to rule the various tribes—this was because when barbarians rebel, strike them; when they submit, soothe them, thereby attaining the principle of supporting the perishing and preserving the existing, without the corvée of distant garrisoning that burdens the people.
translations.idiomatic: In the recent Zhenguan era, after subduing the Nine Surnames, Li Simo was invested as khagan to rule the tribes—when barbarians rebel, strike them; when they submit, soothe them. This upheld the principle of preserving what survives and supporting what is failing, without the burden of distant garrisons.

sentences.zh: 此則近日之令典，經邊之故事。

translations.literal: This is a worthy model of recent times and an established precedent on the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: This is a recent model of good governance and an established frontier precedent.

sentences.zh: 竊見阿史那斛瑟羅，陰山貴種，代雄沙漠，若委之四鎮，使統諸蕃，封為可汗，遣禦寇患，則國家有繼絕之美，荒外無轉輸之役。

translations.literal: I observe that Ashina Huseluo, of noble stock from the Yin Mountains, has been heroic in the desert for generations; if he were entrusted with the four garrisons to rule the various tribes, enfeoffed as khagan, and sent to repel raids, then the state would have the honor of continuing broken lineages, and beyond the wilderness there would be no corvée of transport.
translations.idiomatic: I note that Ashina Huseluo, a noble of the Yin Mountains whose family has been powerful in the desert for generations, could be entrusted with the four garrisons to rule the tribes, enfeoffed as khagan, and charged with repelling raids. The state would gain the honor of restoring broken lineages, and the wilderness beyond would require no supply convoys.

sentences.zh: 如臣所見，請捐四鎮以肥中國，罷安東以實遼西，省軍費於遠方，並甲兵於塞上，則恒、代之鎮重，而邊州之備實矣。

translations.literal: As I see it, I request that the four garrisons be abandoned to enrich the Central Land, Andong be abolished to strengthen Liaoxi, military expenses in distant places be reduced, and armor and troops be concentrated on the frontier—then the garrisons at Heng and Dai would be strengthened, and the defenses of the border prefectures would be made solid.
translations.idiomatic: As I see it, abandon the four garrisons to strengthen the heartland, abolish Andong to fortify Liaoxi, cut military costs in distant lands, and concentrate armor and troops on the frontier. Then the garrisons at Heng and Dai would be reinforced and the border prefectures properly defended.

sentences.zh: 況綏撫夷狄，蓋防其越逸，無侵侮之患則可矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, in soothing and comforting the barbarians, one need only guard against their crossing bounds; if there is no trouble of invasion and insult, that is enough.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in pacifying the barbarians one need only prevent them from crossing the frontier; freedom from raids and aggression is sufficient.

sentences.zh: 何必窮其窟穴，與螻蟻計校長短哉！

translations.literal: Why must one exhaust their dens and measure lengths and shorts with ants!
translations.idiomatic: Why must we hunt them to their lairs and haggle over every inch of ground with them as if they were ants!

sentences.zh: 且王者外寧必有內憂，蓋為不勤修政故也。

translations.literal: Moreover, when a king has external peace, he must have internal worry—this is because he does not diligently cultivate government.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when a ruler enjoys external peace, internal troubles follow—and this is because he fails to govern diligently.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下棄之度外，無以絕域未平為念。

translations.literal: Humbly I consider that Your Majesty should set this beyond concern and not worry that distant regions remain unpacified.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly ask Your Majesty to set this matter aside and not fret over distant lands still unrestored.

sentences.zh: 但當敕邊兵謹守備，蓄銳以待敵，待其自至，然後擊之，此李牧所以製匈奴也。

translations.literal: One need only order the frontier troops to guard carefully, store sharpness and await the enemy, wait until they come of themselves, and then strike them—this is how Li Mu controlled the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: Simply order the frontier troops to hold their defenses, keep their strength in reserve, wait for the enemy to come to them, and then strike—this is how Li Mu mastered the Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: 當今所要者，莫若令邊城警守備，遠斥候，聚軍實，蓄威武。

translations.literal: What is needed now is nothing so much as ordering the border cities to remain alert in defense, posting distant scouts, gathering military supplies, and storing martial might.
translations.idiomatic: What is needed now above all is to keep border cities on alert, post distant scouts, stockpile military supplies, and store up martial strength.

sentences.zh: 以逸待勞，則戰士力倍；

translations.literal: Awaiting the weary with rested troops, the warriors' strength is doubled;
translations.idiomatic: Meeting a weary enemy with rested troops doubles the warriors' strength;

sentences.zh: 以主禦客，則我得其便；

translations.literal: the host defending against the guest, then we gain the advantage;
translations.idiomatic: fighting on home ground against an invader, we hold the advantage;

sentences.zh: 堅壁清野，則寇無所得。

translations.literal: fortifying walls and clearing the countryside, then the raiders gain nothing.
translations.idiomatic: fortifying walls and clearing the fields, the raiders gain nothing.

sentences.zh: 自然賊深入必有顛躓之慮，淺入必無虜獲之益。

translations.literal: Naturally, if bandits penetrate deeply they must have fears of stumbling; if they enter shallowly they certainly gain no benefit from plunder.
translations.idiomatic: Naturally, if raiders push deep they will fear disaster; if they raid shallowly they will gain nothing worth the effort.

sentences.zh: 如此數年，可使二虜不擊而服矣。

translations.literal: After several years like this, one can make the two barbarians submit without striking them.
translations.idiomatic: After several years of this, the two barbarian powers can be made to submit without a blow being struck.

sentences.zh: 仁傑又請廢安東，復高氏為君長，停江南之轉輸，慰河北之勞弊，數年之後，可以安人富國。

translations.literal: Renjie also requested abolishing Andong, restoring the Gao clan as chieftains, stopping transport from the lands south of the Yangtze, and relieving the exhaustion of Hebei—after several years, the people could be secured and the state enriched.
translations.idiomatic: Renjie also proposed abolishing Andong, restoring the Gao clan as local rulers, halting supply convoys from south of the Yangtze, and easing the burdens on Hebei—within a few years the people could be settled and the state made prosperous.

sentences.zh: 事雖不行，識者是之。

translations.literal: Although the proposal was not adopted, those who understood approved it.
translations.idiomatic: Though the proposal was not adopted, those who understood the matter approved of it.

sentences.zh: 尋檢校納言，兼右肅政台御史大夫。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed acting director of memorials and concurrently censor-in-chief of the Right Su Zheng Platform.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed acting director of memorials and concurrently censor-in-chief of the Right Su Zheng Platform.

sentences.zh: 聖曆初，突厥侵掠趙、定等州，命仁傑為河北道元帥，以便宜從事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Shengli era, the Turks raided Zhao, Ding, and other prefectures; Renjie was ordered to serve as commander of the Hebei Circuit with discretionary authority.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Shengli era, Turks raided Zhao, Ding, and other prefectures; Renjie was appointed commander of the Hebei Circuit with full discretionary powers.

sentences.zh: 突厥盡殺所掠男女萬餘人，從五回道而去。

translations.literal: The Turks killed all the more than ten thousand men and women they had captured and departed by the Wuhui Road.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks slaughtered all of the more than ten thousand men and women they had captured and withdrew by the Wuhui Road.

sentences.zh: 仁傑總兵十萬追之不及。

translations.literal: Renjie commanded one hundred thousand troops in pursuit but could not overtake them.
translations.idiomatic: Renjie led one hundred thousand troops in pursuit but failed to catch them.

sentences.zh: 便製仁傑河北道安撫大使。

translations.literal: He was then appointed Renjie pacification commissioner of the Hebei Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Renjie was then appointed pacification commissioner of the Hebei Circuit.

sentences.zh: 時河朔人庶，多為突厥逼脅，賊退後懼誅，又多逃匿。

translations.literal: At that time the people of Hebei, many of them coerced by the Turks, feared punishment after the bandits withdrew and many fled and hid themselves.
translations.idiomatic: At that time many people in Hebei had been coerced by the Turks; after the raiders withdrew they feared punishment and fled into hiding.

sentences.zh: 仁傑上疏曰：

translations.literal: Renjie submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Renjie submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 臣聞朝廷議者，以為契丹作梗，始明人之逆順，或因迫脅，或有願從，或受偽官，或為招慰，或兼外賊，或是土人，跡雖不同，心則無別。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard those debating at court say that because the Khitan caused trouble, one must first clarify whether people were rebellious or loyal—some because of coercion, some willingly following, some accepting false office, some serving as recruiters, some mixed with foreign bandits, some local people; though their tracks differ, in heart there is no distinction.
translations.idiomatic: I hear court debaters say that because the Khitan rebellion has stirred trouble, we must first distinguish loyalty from rebellion—some were coerced, some followed willingly, some accepted offices from the rebels, some served as recruiters, some joined foreign raiders, some were local people. Their circumstances differ, but in intent they are the same.

sentences.zh: 誠以山東雄猛，由來重氣，一顧之勢，至死不回。

translations.literal: Truly the people of Shandong are bold and fierce; they have always valued honor; once committed to a course, they do not turn back even unto death.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Shandong are bold and fierce by nature and have always prized honor; once they commit to a course, they do not turn back even unto death.

sentences.zh: 近緣軍機，調發傷重，家道悉破，或至逃亡，剔屋賣田，人不為售，內顧生計，四壁皆空。

translations.literal: Recently, because of military affairs, levies have gravely harmed them; families have been utterly ruined, some even fleeing; they dismantle houses and sell fields, yet no one will buy; looking inward at their livelihood, all four walls are empty.
translations.idiomatic: Recently military levies have devastated them; families have been ruined, some driven to flight; they tear down houses and sell fields, yet find no buyers; looking at their livelihood, they find nothing left.

sentences.zh: 重以官典侵漁，因事而起，取其髓腦，曾無心愧。

translations.literal: Compounding this, officials extort and plunder, arising opportunistically from events; they take marrow and brains and feel not the slightest shame in heart.
translations.idiomatic: On top of this, officials extort them at every turn, squeezing out everything they have without a shred of shame.

sentences.zh: 修築池城，繕造兵甲，州縣役使，十倍軍機。

translations.literal: Building moats and walls, repairing and making armor and weapons—the corvée demands of prefectures and counties are ten times those of military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Building moats and walls, forging armor and weapons—the corvée levies of prefectures and counties are ten times the military burden.

sentences.zh: 官司不矜，期之必取，枷杖之下，痛切肌膚。

translations.literal: Officials show no compassion; deadlines must be met; under cangue and rod, pain cuts to the flesh.
translations.idiomatic: Officials show no mercy; deadlines must be met; under cangue and rod, pain cuts to the bone.

sentences.zh: 事迫情危，不循禮義，愁苦之地，不樂其生。

translations.literal: Affairs press and emotions are perilous; ritual and righteousness are not followed; in a place of grief and bitterness, one does not delight in life.
translations.idiomatic: Driven to desperation, people abandon propriety; in their misery they no longer cherish life.

sentences.zh: 有利則歸，且圖賒死，此乃君子之愧辱，小人之常行。

translations.literal: Where there is profit they join; they scheme only to delay death—this is a gentleman's shame and a small man's usual conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Where there is advantage they will go; they seek only to postpone death—this is a gentleman's shame and a common man's habit.

sentences.zh: 人猶水也，壅之則為泉，疏之則為川，通塞隨流，豈有常性。

translations.literal: People are like water: dam them and they become a spring; clear them and they become a river; open or blocked, they follow the flow—how could they have a fixed nature?
translations.idiomatic: People are like water: block them and they burst forth as a spring; clear the way and they flow as a river. They follow the course of events—how can they have a fixed nature?

sentences.zh: 昔董卓之亂，神器播遷，及卓被誅，部曲無赦，事窮變起，毒害生人，京室丘墟，化為禾黍。

translations.literal: Formerly in Dong Zhuo's rebellion the imperial regalia was scattered; when Zhuo was executed his followers were not pardoned; affairs reached their limit and change arose; poison harmed the living; the capital became ruins and turned to millet fields.
translations.idiomatic: In Dong Zhuo's rebellion the imperial regalia was cast into chaos; when Zhuo was executed his followers received no pardon. Affairs reached a breaking point and disaster followed; poison spread among the people, and the capital became ruins overgrown with millet.

sentences.zh: 此由恩不普洽，失在機先。

translations.literal: This was because grace was not universally applied; the failure lay in missing the moment beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: This came of grace not reaching all in time—the failure lay in acting too late.

sentences.zh: 臣一讀此書，未嚐不廢卷歎息。

translations.literal: Your subject, each time he reads this account, never fails to put down the scroll and sigh.
translations.idiomatic: Each time I read this account, I cannot help but put down the scroll and sigh.

sentences.zh: 今以負罪之伍，必不在家，露宿草行，潛竄山澤。

translations.literal: Now those bearing guilt surely are not at home; they sleep in the open and travel through grass, secretly hiding in mountains and marshes.
translations.idiomatic: Those who bear guilt now surely do not remain at home; they sleep in the open, travel by stealth through the grass, and hide in mountains and marshes.

sentences.zh: 赦之則出，不赦則狂，山東群盜，緣茲聚結。

translations.literal: If pardoned they will emerge; if not pardoned they will run wild; bandit gangs in Shandong gather and unite for this reason.
translations.idiomatic: Pardon them and they will come forth; withhold pardon and they will run wild—the bandit gangs of Shandong are gathering for this very reason.

sentences.zh: 臣以邊塵暫起，不足為憂，中土不安，以此為事。

translations.literal: Your subject considers that frontier dust rising briefly is not worth worry; unrest in the Central Land is what matters.
translations.idiomatic: I consider brief frontier disturbances no cause for alarm; unrest in the heartland is what truly matters.

sentences.zh: 臣聞持大國者不可以小道，理事廣者不可以細分。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that one who holds a great state cannot use petty methods, and one who governs broadly cannot subdivide finely.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that one who holds a great state cannot govern by petty means, and one who governs on a broad scale cannot rule by fine distinctions.

sentences.zh: 人主恢弘，不拘常法，罪之則眾情恐懼，恕之則反側自安。

translations.literal: A ruler who is magnanimous is not bound by usual law; if he punishes, the feelings of the masses are filled with fear; if he pardons, the rebellious calm themselves.
translations.idiomatic: A magnanimous ruler is not bound by ordinary law; punish and the people will tremble with fear; pardon and the disaffected will settle of their own accord.

sentences.zh: 伏願曲赦河北諸州，一無所問。

translations.literal: Humbly I wish that a special pardon be granted to the prefectures of Hebei, questioning nothing at all.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly ask that a special amnesty be granted to all the prefectures of Hebei, with no questions asked.

sentences.zh: 自然人神道暢，率土歡心，諸軍凱旋，得無侵擾。

translations.literal: By nature Heaven and the Way are unobstructed; the whole land rejoices in heart; the armies return in triumph; there will be no harassment.
translations.idiomatic: When Heaven and the Way are in harmony, the whole realm rejoices; as the armies return in triumph, there will be no harassment.

sentences.zh: 製從之。

translations.literal: The edict followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved this.

sentences.zh: 軍還，授內史。

translations.literal: The army returned; he was appointed Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, he was appointed Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 聖曆三年，則天幸三陽宮，王公百僚鹹經侍從，唯仁傑特賜宅一區，當時恩寵無比。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shenli, Empress Wu visited the Sanyang Palace; princes, dukes, and the hundred officials all accompanied her on the journey; only Di Renjie was specially granted one entire residence—favor at the time without parallel.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Shenli, Empress Wu visited the Sanyang Palace; princes, dukes, and all officials accompanied her on the journey; only Di Renjie was specially granted an entire residence—a favor without parallel at the time.

sentences.zh: 是歲六月，左玉鈐衛大將軍李楷固、右武威衛將軍駱務整討契丹餘眾，擒之，獻俘於含樞殿。

translations.literal: That year in the sixth month, Left Jade Clasp Guard General Li Kaigu and Right Martial Prestige Guard General Luo Wuzheng pursued the remaining Khitan forces, captured them, and presented captives at the Hanyu Hall.
translations.idiomatic: That year in the sixth month, Left Jade Clasp Guard General Li Kaigu and Right Martial Prestige Guard General Luo Wuzheng pursued the remaining Khitan forces, captured them, and presented the captives at the Hanyu Hall.

sentences.zh: 則天大悅，特賜楷固姓武氏。

translations.literal: Empress Wu was greatly pleased and specially granted Kaigu the surname Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu was greatly pleased and specially granted Kaigu the surname Wu.

sentences.zh: 楷固、務整，並契丹李盡忠之別帥也。

translations.literal: Kaigu and Wuzheng were both deputy commanders under the Khitan Li Jinzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Kaigu and Wuzheng were both deputy commanders under the Khitan Li Jinzhong.

sentences.zh: 初，盡忠之作亂，楷固等屢率兵以陷官軍，後兵敗來降，有司斷以極法。

translations.literal: Initially, when Jinzhong rebelled, Kaigu and the others repeatedly led troops to defeat government forces; later, after defeat, they came to surrender; the authorities judged them by the extreme penalty.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, when Jinzhong rebelled, Kaigu and the others repeatedly led troops to defeat the government forces; later, after their defeat, they came to surrender, and the authorities judged them according to the extreme penalty.

sentences.zh: 仁傑議以為楷固等並有驍將之才，若恕其死，必能感恩效節。

translations.literal: Di Renjie argued that Kaigu and the others all had the talent of fierce generals; if their deaths were pardoned, they would surely be grateful and devote themselves in loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Di Renjie argued that Kaigu and the others all possessed the talent of fierce generals; if their lives were spared, they would surely be grateful and devote themselves to service.

sentences.zh: 又奏請授其官爵，委以專征。

translations.literal: He further memorialized requesting that they be granted office and rank and entrusted with independent command.
translations.idiomatic: He further memorialized requesting that they be granted office and rank and entrusted with independent command.

sentences.zh: 製並從之。

translations.literal: The edict approved all of this.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved all of this.

sentences.zh: 及楷固等凱旋，則天召仁傑預宴，因舉觴親勸，歸賞於仁傑。

translations.literal: When Kaigu and the others returned in triumph, Empress Wu summoned Di Renjie to the banquet, raised her cup to toast him personally, and attributed the credit to Di Renjie.
translations.idiomatic: When Kaigu and the others returned in triumph, Empress Wu summoned Di Renjie to the banquet, raised her cup to toast him personally, and attributed the credit to Di Renjie.

sentences.zh: 授楷固左玉鈐衛大將軍，賜爵燕國公。

translations.literal: Kaigu was appointed Left Jade Clasp Guard General and granted the title Duke of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Kaigu was appointed Left Jade Clasp Guard General and granted the title Duke of Yan.

sentences.zh: 則天又將造大像，用功數百萬，令天下僧尼每日人出一錢，以助成之。

translations.literal: Empress Wu also planned to erect a great image, requiring millions of work-days; she ordered all monks and nuns in the realm to contribute one coin per person per day to help complete it.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu also planned to erect a great Buddha image, requiring millions of work-days; she ordered all monks and nuns in the realm to contribute one coin per person per day to help complete it.

sentences.zh: 仁傑上疏諫曰：

translations.literal: Di Renjie submitted a memorial of remonstrance, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Di Renjie submitted a memorial of remonstrance, saying:

sentences.zh: 臣聞為政之本，必先人事。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that the foundation of governing lies first in human affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject has heard that the foundation of governing lies first in attending to human affairs.

sentences.zh: 陛下矜群生迷謬，溺喪無歸，欲令像教兼行，睹相生善。

translations.literal: Your Majesty pities living beings lost in error, drowned in misery with nowhere to turn, and wishes that the religion of images be practiced alongside other teachings, so that seeing images may give rise to goodness.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty pities living beings lost in error, drowned in misery with nowhere to turn, and wishes that the religion of images be practiced alongside other teachings, so that people seeing images may be moved to do good.

sentences.zh: 非為塔廟必欲崇奢，豈令僧尼皆須檀施？

translations.literal: It is not that pagodas and temples must necessarily be made luxurious—surely Your Majesty does not mean that all monks and nuns must rely on donations?
translations.idiomatic: It is not that pagodas and temples must necessarily be made luxurious—surely Your Majesty does not mean that all monks and nuns must rely on donations?

sentences.zh: 得栰尚舍，而況其餘。

translations.literal: Even when obtaining rafters one still holds back—how much more the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Even when cutting timber for rafters one still holds back—how much more everything else.

sentences.zh: 今之伽藍，製過宮闕，窮奢極壯，畫繢盡工，寶珠殫於綴飾，環材竭於輪奐。

translations.literal: Today's monasteries surpass the palace in scale—extravagant beyond measure, painted with utmost artistry; precious pearls are exhausted in ornamentation, and fine timber is depleted in ornate construction.
translations.idiomatic: Today's monasteries surpass the palace in scale—extravagant beyond measure, painted with utmost artistry; precious pearls are exhausted in ornamentation, and fine timber is depleted in ornate construction.

sentences.zh: 工不使鬼，止在役人，物不天來，終須地出，不損百姓，將何以求？

translations.literal: Labor does not employ ghosts—it falls only on conscripted men; goods do not come from Heaven—they must ultimately come from the earth. Without burdening the common people, from what source are these to be obtained?
translations.idiomatic: Ghosts do not perform the labor—it falls entirely on conscripted men; goods do not fall from heaven—they must ultimately come from the earth. Without burdening the common people, from what source are these to be obtained?

sentences.zh: 生之有時，用之無度，編戶所奉，常若不充，痛切肌膚，不辭箠楚。

translations.literal: Life has its seasons, yet expenditure knows no bounds; what registered households provide is constantly insufficient; the pain cuts to the flesh, yet they do not shrink from the lash.
translations.idiomatic: Life has its seasons, yet expenditure knows no bounds; what registered households provide is constantly insufficient; the pain cuts to the flesh, yet they do not shrink from the lash.

sentences.zh: 遊僧一說，矯陳禍福，翦發解衣，仍慚其少。

translations.literal: A wandering monk speaks once, falsely proclaiming fortune and disaster; people shave their heads and strip off their clothes, yet still feel ashamed that their gifts are too small.
translations.idiomatic: A wandering monk speaks once, falsely proclaiming fortune and disaster; people shave their heads and strip off their clothes, yet still feel ashamed that their gifts are too small.

sentences.zh: 亦有離間骨肉，事均路人，身自納妻，謂無彼我。

translations.literal: Some even sunder flesh and blood, treating family as strangers would; monks themselves take wives, claiming there is no distinction between self and other.
translations.idiomatic: Some even sunder flesh and blood, treating family as strangers would; monks themselves take wives, claiming there is no distinction between self and other.

sentences.zh: 皆托佛法，詿誤生人。

translations.literal: All resort to the Buddhist Dharma to deceive and mislead the living.
translations.idiomatic: All resort to the Buddhist Dharma to deceive and mislead the living.

sentences.zh: 裏陌動有經坊，闤闠亦立精舍。

translations.literal: Within every lane there are scripture halls; in every marketplace monasteries are erected.
translations.idiomatic: Within every lane there are scripture halls; in every marketplace monasteries are erected.

sentences.zh: 化誘倍急，切於官征；

translations.literal: Fundraising is twice as pressing as official levies;
translations.idiomatic: Fundraising is twice as pressing as official levies;

sentences.zh: 法事所須，嚴於製敕。

translations.literal: Requirements for Buddhist rites are stricter than imperial edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Requirements for Buddhist rites are stricter than imperial edicts.

sentences.zh: 膏腴美業，倍取其多；

translations.literal: Fertile, profitable lands—they take double shares;
translations.idiomatic: They take double shares of fertile, profitable lands;

sentences.zh: 水碾莊園，數亦非少。

translations.literal: Water mills and estate manors—the number is likewise not small.
translations.idiomatic: Water mills and estate manors—the number is likewise not small.

sentences.zh: 逃丁避罪，並集法門，無名之僧，凡有幾萬，都下檢括，已得數千。

translations.literal: Draft evaders and fugitives from justice all flock to Buddhist temples; nameless monks number tens of thousands—in the capital alone, several thousand have already been counted in the census.
translations.idiomatic: Draft evaders and fugitives from justice all flock to Buddhist temples; nameless monks number tens of thousands—in the capital alone, several thousand have already been counted in the census.

sentences.zh: 且一夫不耕，猶受其弊，浮食者眾，又劫人財。

translations.literal: Moreover, if even one man does not plow, all still suffer the loss; those who live idly are many, and they further plunder people's wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, if even one man does not plow, all still suffer the loss; those who live idly are many, and they further plunder people's wealth.

sentences.zh: 臣每思惟，實所悲痛。

translations.literal: Each time your subject reflects on this, he is truly grieved.
translations.idiomatic: Each time your subject reflects on this, he is truly grieved.

sentences.zh: 往在江表，像法盛興，梁武、簡文，舍施無限。

translations.literal: Formerly in the lands south of the Yangtze, the Buddhist religion flourished; Emperor Wu and Emperor Jianwen of Liang gave donations without limit.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly in the lands south of the Yangtze, the Buddhist religion flourished; Emperor Wu and Emperor Jianwen of Liang gave donations without limit.

sentences.zh: 及其三淮沸浪，五嶺騰煙。

translations.literal: Yet when the Three Huai seethed like boiling waves and the Five Ridges blazed with smoke.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when the Three Huai seethed like boiling waves and the Five Ridges blazed with smoke.

sentences.zh: 列刹盈衢，無救危亡之禍；

translations.literal: Monasteries lined the streets in abundance, yet could not avert the disaster of ruin;
translations.idiomatic: Monasteries lined the streets in abundance, yet could not avert the disaster of ruin;

sentences.zh: 緇衣蔽路，豈有勤王之師！

translations.literal: Monks in black robes covered the roads—where were the armies that would rally to save the throne!
translations.idiomatic: Monks in black robes covered the roads—where were the armies that would rally to save the throne!

sentences.zh: 比年已來，風塵屢擾，水旱不節，征役稍繁。

translations.literal: In recent years war has repeatedly disturbed the realm; floods and droughts have come out of season; corvée and levies have grown somewhat heavy.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years war has repeatedly disturbed the realm; floods and droughts have come out of season; corvée and levies have grown somewhat heavy.
