sentences.zh: 家業先空，瘡痍未復，此時興役，力所未堪，伏惟聖朝，功德無量，何必要營大像，而以勞費為名。

translations.literal: Household estates are already emptied; wounds are not yet healed—at such a time to launch a major project is more than strength can bear. Humbly considering the holy dynasty's boundless merit, why must a great image be built, taking labor and expense as its name.
translations.idiomatic: Household estates are already emptied; wounds are not yet healed—at such a time to launch a major project is more than strength can bear. Humbly considering the holy dynasty's boundless merit, why must a great image be built, taking labor and expense as its name.

sentences.zh: 雖斂僧錢，百未支一。

translations.literal: Even collecting money from monks, not one part in a hundred would suffice.
translations.idiomatic: Even collecting money from monks, not one part in a hundred would suffice.

sentences.zh: 尊容既廣，不可露居，覆以百層，尚憂未遍，自餘廓廡，不得全無。

translations.literal: The sacred image being so vast, it cannot stand exposed; even a hundred layers of roofing would still leave one anxious it is not covered enough—and the surrounding halls and galleries cannot be dispensed with entirely.
translations.idiomatic: The sacred image being so vast, it cannot stand exposed; even a hundred layers of roofing would still leave one anxious it is not covered enough—and the surrounding halls and galleries cannot be dispensed with entirely.

sentences.zh: 又雲不損國財，不傷百姓，以此事主，可謂盡忠？

translations.literal: Yet it is also said that state revenue will not be harmed and the common people will not suffer—is this what may be called serving one's lord with full loyalty?
translations.idiomatic: Yet it is also said that state revenue will not be harmed and the common people will not suffer—is this what may be called serving one's lord with full loyalty?

sentences.zh: 臣今思惟，兼采眾議，鹹以為如來設教，以慈悲為主，下濟群品，應是本心，豈欲勞人，以存虛飾？

translations.literal: Your subject now reflects, having also gathered common opinion—all agree that when the Tathagata established his teaching, compassion was paramount, descending to save all beings—this should be the original intent. Would he wish to burden people merely to preserve empty ornament?
translations.idiomatic: Your subject now reflects, having also gathered common opinion—all agree that when the Tathagata established his teaching, compassion was paramount, descending to save all beings—this should be the original intent. Would he wish to burden people merely to preserve empty ornament?

sentences.zh: 當今有事，邊境未寧，宜寬征鎮之徭，省不急之費。

translations.literal: Now there are pressing affairs; the frontiers are not yet calm. It is fitting to ease levies and corvée on the garrison regions and reduce expenditures that are not urgent.
translations.idiomatic: Now there are pressing affairs; the frontiers are not yet calm. It is fitting to ease levies and corvée on the garrison regions and reduce expenditures that are not urgent.

sentences.zh: 設令雇作，皆以利趨，既失田時，自然棄本。

translations.literal: Even if labor were hired, all would be drawn by profit; missing the season for planting, they would naturally abandon the fundamental occupation.
translations.idiomatic: Even if labor were hired, all would be drawn by profit; missing the season for planting, they would naturally abandon the fundamental occupation.

sentences.zh: 今不樹稼，來歲必饑，役在其中，難以取給。

translations.literal: If crops are not planted now, next year famine is certain; corvée labor lies among these troubles—how can supplies be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: If crops are not planted now, next year famine is certain; corvée labor lies among these troubles—how can supplies be obtained.

sentences.zh: 況無官助，義無得成，若費官財，又盡人力，一隅有難，將何救之！

translations.literal: Moreover, without government aid the project cannot rightly be completed; if state funds are spent and human labor exhausted, when difficulty arises in one corner, with what shall it be met!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, without government aid the project cannot rightly be completed; if state funds are spent and human labor exhausted, when difficulty arises in one corner, with what shall it be met!

sentences.zh: 則天乃罷其役。

translations.literal: Empress Wu then canceled the project.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu then canceled the project.

sentences.zh: 是歲九月，病卒，則天為之舉哀，廢朝三日，贈文昌右相，諡曰文惠。

translations.literal: That year in the ninth month he died of illness. Empress Wu mourned him, suspended court for three days, posthumously appointed him Right Vice Minister of the Secretariat, and gave him the posthumous name Wenhui.
translations.idiomatic: That year in the ninth month he died of illness. Empress Wu mourned him, suspended court for three days, posthumously appointed him Right Vice Minister of the Secretariat, and gave him the posthumous name Wenhui.

sentences.zh: 仁傑常以舉賢為意，其所引拔桓彥範、敬暉、竇懷貞、姚崇等，至公卿者數十人。

translations.literal: Di Renjie always made recommending the worthy his purpose; those he promoted—Huan Yanfan, Jing Hui, Dou Huaizhen, Yao Chong, and others—who reached ministerial rank numbered several dozen.
translations.idiomatic: Di Renjie always made recommending the worthy his purpose; those he promoted—Huan Yanfan, Jing Hui, Dou Huaizhen, Yao Chong, and others—who reached ministerial rank numbered several dozen.

sentences.zh: 初，則天嚐問仁傑曰：“朕要一好漢任使，有乎？”

translations.literal: Initially, Empress Wu once asked Di Renjie: "I need a capable man to employ—is there one?"
translations.idiomatic: Initially, Empress Wu once asked Di Renjie: "I need a capable man to employ—is there one?"

sentences.zh: 仁傑曰：“陛下作何任使？”

translations.literal: Di Renjie said: "For what employment does Your Majesty intend him?"
translations.idiomatic: Di Renjie said: "For what employment does Your Majesty intend him?"

sentences.zh: 則天曰：“朕欲待以將相。”

translations.literal: Empress Wu said: "I wish to treat him as a general or minister."
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu said: "I wish to treat him as a general or minister."

sentences.zh: 對曰：“臣料陛下若求文章資曆，則今之宰臣李嶠、蘇味道亦足為文吏矣。

translations.literal: He replied: "Your subject supposes that if Your Majesty seeks literary credentials, the present chief ministers Li Jiao and Su Weidao would suffice as literary officials.
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "Your subject supposes that if Your Majesty seeks literary credentials, the present chief ministers Li Jiao and Su Weidao would suffice as literary officials.

sentences.zh: 豈非文士齷齪，思得奇才用之，以成天下之務者乎？”

translations.literal: Is it not that literary men seem petty, and Your Majesty wishes to obtain extraordinary talent to accomplish the affairs of the realm?"
translations.idiomatic: Is it not that literary men seem petty, and Your Majesty wishes to obtain extraordinary talent to accomplish the affairs of the realm?"

sentences.zh: 則天悅曰：“此朕心也。”

translations.literal: Empress Wu said happily: "This is exactly my mind."
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu said happily: "This is exactly my mind."

sentences.zh: 仁傑曰：“荊州長史張柬之，其人雖老，真宰相才也。

translations.literal: Di Renjie said: "Zhang Jianzhi, long secretary of Jingzhou—though old in years, he is truly ministerial timber.
translations.idiomatic: Di Renjie said: "Zhang Jianzhi, long secretary of Jingzhou—though old in years, he is truly ministerial timber.

sentences.zh: 且久不遇，若用之，必盡節於國家矣。”

translations.literal: Moreover, he has long gone unrecognized; if employed, he would surely devote his utmost to the state."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, he has long gone unrecognized; if employed, he would surely devote his utmost to the state."

sentences.zh: 則天乃召拜洛州司馬。

translations.literal: Empress Wu then summoned him and appointed him Vice Prefect of Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu then summoned him and appointed him Vice Prefect of Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 他日，又求賢。

translations.literal: Another day she again sought able men.
translations.idiomatic: Another day she again sought able men.

sentences.zh: 仁傑曰：“臣前言張柬之，猶未用也。”

translations.literal: Di Renjie said: "Your subject spoke earlier of Zhang Jianzhi—he has still not been properly employed."
translations.idiomatic: Di Renjie said: "Your subject spoke earlier of Zhang Jianzhi—he has still not been properly employed."

sentences.zh: 則天曰：“已遷之矣。”

translations.literal: Empress Wu said: "He has already been transferred."
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu said: "He has already been transferred."

sentences.zh: 對曰：“臣薦之為相，今為洛州司馬，非用之也。”

translations.literal: He replied: "Your subject recommended him as chancellor; now he is Vice Prefect of Luozhou—that is not employing him."
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "Your subject recommended him as chancellor; now he is Vice Prefect of Luozhou—that is not employing him."

sentences.zh: 又遷為秋官侍郎，後竟召為相。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Vice Minister of Justice; eventually he was summoned to serve as chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: He was again transferred to Vice Minister of Justice; eventually he was summoned to serve as chancellor.

sentences.zh: 柬之果能興復中宗，蓋仁傑之推薦也。

translations.literal: Zhang Jianzhi indeed restored Emperor Zhongzong—a result of Di Renjie's recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jianzhi indeed restored Emperor Zhongzong—a result of Di Renjie's recommendation.

sentences.zh: 仁傑嚐為魏州刺史，人吏為立生祠。

translations.literal: Di Renjie once served as prefect of Weizhou; officials and people erected a living shrine to him.
translations.idiomatic: Di Renjie once served as prefect of Weizhou; officials and people erected a living shrine to him.

sentences.zh: 及去職，其子景暉為魏州司功參軍，頗貪暴，為人所惡，乃毀仁傑之祠。

translations.literal: When he left office, his son Jinghui served as judicial aide of Weizhou; he was quite greedy and brutal, hated by the people, and so they destroyed Di Renjie's shrine.
translations.idiomatic: When he left office, his son Jinghui served as judicial aide of Weizhou; he was quite greedy and brutal, hated by the people, and so they destroyed Di Renjie's shrine.

sentences.zh: 長子光嗣，聖曆初為司府丞，則天令宰相各舉尚書郎一人，仁傑乃薦光嗣。

translations.literal: His eldest son Guangsi, at the beginning of Shenli, served as aide in the Ministry of Revenue. Empress Wu ordered each chancellor to recommend one Secretariat director; Di Renjie recommended Guangsi.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Guangsi, at the beginning of Shenli, served as aide in the Ministry of Revenue. Empress Wu ordered each chancellor to recommend one Secretariat director; Di Renjie recommended Guangsi.

sentences.zh: 拜地官員外郎，蒞事稱職，則天喜而言曰：“祁奚內舉，果得其人。”

translations.literal: He was appointed vice director in the Ministry of Revenue; in discharging his duties he proved competent. Empress Wu said with pleasure: "Like Qi Xi recommending from within his own family, he has indeed found the right man."
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed vice director in the Ministry of Revenue; in discharging his duties he proved competent. Empress Wu said with pleasure: "Like Qi Xi recommending from within his own family, he has indeed found the right man."

sentences.zh: 開元七年，自汴州刺史轉揚州大都督府長史，坐贓貶歙州別駕卒。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Kaiyuan, transferred from prefect of Bianzhou to chief secretary of the Yangzhou Metropolitan Area Command; convicted of corruption, demoted to vice prefect of Shezhou, where he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Kaiyuan, transferred from prefect of Bianzhou to chief secretary of the Yangzhou Metropolitan Area Command; convicted of corruption, demoted to vice prefect of Shezhou, where he died.

sentences.zh: 初，中宗在房陵，而吉頊、李昭德皆有匡復讜言，則天無復辟意。

translations.literal: Initially, while Emperor Zhongzong was at Fangling, Ji Xu and Li Zhaode both had plans for restoration, but Empress Wu had no intention of restoring him.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, while Emperor Zhongzong was at Fangling, Ji Xu and Li Zhaode both had plans for restoration, but Empress Wu had no intention of restoring him.

sentences.zh: 唯仁傑每從容奏對，無不以子母恩情為言，則天亦漸省悟，竟召還中宗，復為儲貳。

translations.literal: Only Di Renjie, in each calm memorial and reply, spoke invariably of the bond between mother and son; Empress Wu gradually came to understand, and eventually recalled Zhongzong and restored him as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Only Di Renjie, in each calm memorial and reply, spoke invariably of the bond between mother and son; Empress Wu gradually came to understand, and eventually recalled Zhongzong and restored him as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 初，中宗自房陵還宮，則天匿之帳中，召仁傑以廬陵為言。

translations.literal: Initially, when Zhongzong returned from Fangling to the palace, Empress Wu hid him behind a screen and summoned Di Renjie, speaking of the Prince of Luling.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, when Zhongzong returned from Fangling to the palace, Empress Wu hid him behind a screen and summoned Di Renjie, speaking of the Prince of Luling.

sentences.zh: 仁傑慷慨敷奏，言發涕流，遽出中宗謂仁傑曰：“還卿儲君。”

translations.literal: Di Renjie spoke passionately in memorial; tears flowed as he spoke. Empress Wu suddenly brought out Zhongzong and said to Di Renjie: "I restore your crown prince to you."
translations.idiomatic: Di Renjie spoke passionately in memorial; tears flowed as he spoke. Empress Wu suddenly brought out Zhongzong and said to Di Renjie: "I restore your crown prince to you."

sentences.zh: 仁傑降階泣賀，既已，奏曰：“太子還宮，人無知者，物議安審是非？”

translations.literal: Di Renjie descended the steps weeping with congratulations; when that was done, he memorialized: "The crown prince has returned to the palace, yet no one knows of it—how can public opinion judge what is right and wrong?"
translations.idiomatic: Di Renjie descended the steps weeping with congratulations; when that was done, he memorialized: "The crown prince has returned to the palace, yet no one knows of it—how can public opinion judge what is right and wrong?"

sentences.zh: 則天以為然，乃復置中宗於龍門，具禮迎歸，人情感悅。

translations.literal: Empress Wu agreed; she then restored Zhongzong at Longmen Gate with full ceremonial welcome, and the people's hearts were gladdened.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu agreed; she then restored Zhongzong at Longmen Gate with full ceremonial welcome, and the people's hearts were gladdened.

sentences.zh: 仁傑前後匡復奏對，凡數萬言，開元中，北海太守李邕撰為《梁公別傳》，備載其辭。

translations.literal: Di Renjie's memorials and replies on restoration altogether amounted to tens of thousands of words; in the Kaiyuan era, Li Yong, prefect of Beihai, compiled them as the "Separate Biography of the Duke of Liang," recording his words in full.
translations.idiomatic: Di Renjie's memorials and replies on restoration altogether amounted to tens of thousands of words; in the Kaiyuan era, Li Yong, prefect of Beihai, compiled them as the "Separate Biography of the Duke of Liang," recording his words in full.

sentences.zh: 中宗返正，追贈司空；

translations.literal: When Zhongzong restored legitimate rule, Di Renjie was posthumously granted the title of Minister of Works;
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongzong restored legitimate rule, Di Renjie was posthumously granted the title of Minister of Works;

sentences.zh: 睿宗追封梁國公。

translations.literal: Emperor Ruizong posthumously enfeoffed him as Duke of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ruizong posthumously enfeoffed him as Duke of Liang.

sentences.zh: 仁傑族曾孫兼謨。

translations.literal: Di Renjie's collateral great-great-grandson was Jianmo.
translations.idiomatic: Di Renjie's collateral great-great-grandson was Jianmo.

sentences.zh: 兼謨，登進士第。

translations.literal: Jianmo passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Jianmo passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 祖郊、父邁，仕官皆微。

translations.literal: His grandfather Jiao and father Mai both held minor offices.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jiao and father Mai both held minor offices.

sentences.zh: 兼謨元和末解褐襄陽推官，試校書郎，言行剛正，使府知名。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yuanhe era Jianmo began his career as legal aide at Xiangyang, with probationary appointment as collator; upright in word and deed, he became known in the commissionerate.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yuanhe era Jianmo began his career as legal aide at Xiangyang, with probationary appointment as collator; upright in word and deed, he became known in the commissionerate.

sentences.zh: 憲宗召為左拾遺，累上書言事，曆尚書郎。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong summoned him as Left Reminder; he repeatedly submitted memorials on affairs of state and successively served as Secretariat director.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong summoned him as Left Reminder; he repeatedly submitted memorials on affairs of state and successively served as Secretariat director.

sentences.zh: 長慶、太和中，曆鄭州刺史，以治行稱，入為給事中。

translations.literal: During Changqing and Taihe he served as prefect of Zhengzhou, renowned for his governance, and entered the capital as Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: During Changqing and Taihe he served as prefect of Zhengzhou, renowned for his governance, and entered the capital as Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 開成初，度支左藏庫妄破漬汙縑帛等贓罪，文宗以事在赦前不理。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaicheng, officials of the Revenue Bureau's left treasury falsely damaged and spoiled silk goods—a corruption offense; Emperor Wenzong held that since the matter preceded an amnesty, it would not be prosecuted.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Kaicheng, officials of the Revenue Bureau's left treasury falsely damaged and spoiled silk goods—a corruption offense; Emperor Wenzong held that since the matter preceded an amnesty, it would not be prosecuted.

sentences.zh: 兼謨封還敕書，文宗召而諭之曰：“嘉卿舉職，然朕已赦其長官，典吏亦宜在宥。

translations.literal: Jianmo sealed and returned the edict. Emperor Wenzong summoned him and instructed: "I commend your fulfillment of duty; yet I have already pardoned the chief official—the clerks should likewise be forgiven.
translations.idiomatic: Jianmo sealed and returned the edict. Emperor Wenzong summoned him and instructed: "I commend your fulfillment of duty; yet I have already pardoned the chief official—the clerks should likewise be forgiven.

sentences.zh: 然事或不可，卿勿以封敕為艱。”

translations.literal: Yet if matters cannot be accepted, do not find returning edicts difficult."
translations.idiomatic: Yet if matters cannot be accepted, do not find returning edicts difficult."

sentences.zh: 遷御史中丞。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 謝日，文宗顧謂之曰：“御史台朝廷綱紀，台綱正則朝廷理，朝廷正則天下理。

translations.literal: On the day of his formal thanks, Emperor Wenzong turned to him and said: "The Censorate is the discipline of the court; when censorial discipline is upright, the court is well governed; when the court is upright, the realm is well governed.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of his formal thanks, Emperor Wenzong turned to him and said: "The Censorate is the discipline of the court; when censorial discipline is upright, the court is well governed; when the court is upright, the realm is well governed.

sentences.zh: 凡執法者，大抵以畏忌顧望為心，職業由茲不舉。

translations.literal: Those who enforce the law are generally governed by fear, caution, and looking about; duty thereby goes unfulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: Those who enforce the law are generally governed by fear, caution, and looking about; duty thereby goes unfulfilled.

sentences.zh: 卿梁公之後，自有家法，豈復為常常之心哉！”

translations.literal: You are a descendant of the Duke of Liang and have your family's standards—is it not so that you will no longer harbor an ordinary timid heart!"
translations.idiomatic: You are a descendant of the Duke of Liang and have your family's standards—is it not so that you will no longer harbor an ordinary timid heart!"

sentences.zh: 兼謨謝曰：“朝法或未得中，臣固悉心彈奏。”

translations.literal: Jianmo replied: "If court law has not been properly applied, your subject will earnestly memorialize and impeach."
translations.idiomatic: Jianmo replied: "If court law has not been properly applied, your subject will earnestly memorialize and impeach."

sentences.zh: 會江西觀察使吳士矩違額加給軍士，破官錢數十萬計。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward, Jiangxi observation commissioner Wu Shiju exceeded the authorized quota in augmenting soldiers' pay, depleting several hundred thousand in official funds.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward, Jiangxi observation commissioner Wu Shiju exceeded the authorized quota in augmenting soldiers' pay, depleting several hundred thousand in official funds.

sentences.zh: 兼謨奏曰：“觀察使守陛下土地，宣陛下詔條，臨戎賞軍，州有定數。

translations.literal: Jianmo memorialized: "An observation commissioner guards Your Majesty's territory and promulgates Your Majesty's statutes; rewards to troops on campaign have fixed amounts by prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Jianmo memorialized: "An observation commissioner guards Your Majesty's territory and promulgates Your Majesty's statutes; rewards to troops on campaign have fixed amounts by prefecture.

sentences.zh: 而士矩與奪由己，盈縮自專，不唯貽弊一方，必致諸軍援例。

translations.literal: Yet Shiju dispensed and withheld at his own discretion, deciding surpluses and deficits by himself—not only does this harm one region, it will surely lead all armies to cite it as precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Shiju dispensed and withheld at his own discretion, deciding surpluses and deficits by himself—not only does this harm one region, it will surely lead all armies to cite it as precedent.

sentences.zh: 請下法司，正行朝典。”

translations.literal: I request that the matter be referred to the judicial offices so that court statutes may be properly enforced."
translations.idiomatic: I request that the matter be referred to the judicial offices so that court statutes may be properly enforced."

sentences.zh: 士矩坐貶蔡州別駕。

translations.literal: Wu Shiju was convicted and demoted to vice prefect of Caizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shiju was convicted and demoted to vice prefect of Caizhou.

sentences.zh: 兼謨尋轉兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: Jianmo was soon transferred to Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Jianmo was soon transferred to Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 明年，檢校工部尚書、太原尹，充河東節度使。

translations.literal: The following year he served as Acting Minister of Public Works and military governor of Hedong as prefect of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he served as Acting Minister of Public Works and military governor of Hedong as prefect of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 會昌中，累歴方鎮，卒。

translations.literal: During Huichang, he successively served in regional commands and died.
translations.idiomatic: During the Huichang era he successively served in regional commands and died.

sentences.zh: 王方慶，雍州咸陽人也，周少司空石泉公褒之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Wang Fangqing was a native of Xianyang in Yongzhou, the great-grandson of Bao, Duke of Shiquan and Vice Minister of Works under Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fangqing was a native of Xianyang in Yongzhou, the great-grandson of Bao, Duke of Shiquan and Vice Minister of Works under Zhou.

sentences.zh: 其先自琅邪南度，居於丹陽，為江左冠族。

translations.literal: His ancestors crossed south from Langye and settled in Danyang, becoming a leading clan of the Jiangzuo region.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestors crossed south from Langye and settled in Danyang, becoming a leading clan of the Jiangzuo region.

sentences.zh: 褒北徙入關，始家咸陽焉。

translations.literal: Bao moved north into the passes and first established the family at Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: Bao moved north into the passes and first established the family at Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 祖鼒，隋衛尉丞。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zi served as aide in the Ministry of Guardians under Sui.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zi served as aide in the Ministry of Guardians under Sui.

sentences.zh: 伯父弘讓，有美名，貞觀中為中書舍人。

translations.literal: His father's elder brother Hongrang had a fine reputation and served as Secretariat drafter during the Zhenguan era.
translations.idiomatic: His father's elder brother Hongrang had a fine reputation and served as Secretariat drafter during the Zhenguan era.

sentences.zh: 父弘直，為漢王元昌友，畋獵無度，乃上書切諫，其略曰：“夫宗子維城之托者，所以固邦家之業也。

translations.literal: His father Hongzhi served as companion to Prince Yuan of Han; the prince hunted without restraint, so Hongzhi submitted a stern memorial of remonstrance, in summary saying: "The charge entrusted to a prince of the blood is to buttress the realm like a city wall and thereby secure the enterprise of state and family.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hongzhi served as companion to Prince Yuan of Han; the prince hunted without restraint, so Hongzhi submitted a stern memorial of remonstrance, in summary saying: "The charge entrusted to a prince of the blood is to buttress the realm like a city wall and thereby secure the enterprise of state and family.

sentences.zh: 大王功無任城戰克之效，行無河間樂善之譽，爵高五等，邑富千室，當思答極施之洪慈，保無疆之永祚。

translations.literal: Your Highness has no achievement like the victory at Rencheng in battle, no reputation like the Prince of Hejian's love of virtue; your rank is among the five highest, your fief rich with a thousand households—you should reflect on repaying the supreme sovereign's vast grace and preserving an everlasting fortune without end.
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness has no achievement like the victory at Rencheng in battle, no reputation like the Prince of Hejian's love of virtue; your rank is among the five highest, your fief rich with a thousand households—you should reflect on repaying the supreme sovereign's vast grace and preserving an everlasting fortune without end.

sentences.zh: 其為計者，在乎修德，冠屨《詩》《禮》，畋獵史傳。

translations.literal: The plan to follow lies in cultivating virtue—cap and shoes in the Odes and Rites, hunting only in the histories and chronicles.
translations.idiomatic: The plan to follow lies in cultivating virtue—cap and shoes in the Odes and Rites, hunting only in the histories and chronicles.

sentences.zh: 覽古人成敗之所由，鑒既往存亡之異跡，覆前戒後，居安慮危。

translations.literal: Read why the ancients succeeded or failed; take as mirror the differing traces of past survival and ruin; overturn what came before to warn what follows; in security consider peril.
translations.idiomatic: Read why the ancients succeeded or failed; take as mirror the differing traces of past survival and ruin; overturn what came before to warn what follows; in security consider peril.

sentences.zh: 奈何列騎齊驅，交橫壟畝，野有遊客，巷無居人。

translations.literal: Yet how is it that ranks of horsemen drive abreast, crossing the furrows of the fields—travelers in the wilds, no residents in the lanes?
translations.idiomatic: Yet how is it that ranks of horsemen drive abreast, crossing the furrows of the fields—travelers in the wilds, no residents in the lanes?

sentences.zh: 貽眾庶之憂，逞一情之樂，從禽不息，實用寒心。”

translations.literal: You bequeath worry to the multitude yet indulge a single pleasure; pursuit of game without cease truly chills the heart."
translations.idiomatic: You bequeath worry to the multitude yet indulge a single pleasure; pursuit of game without cease truly chills the heart."

sentences.zh: 元昌覽書而遽止。

translations.literal: Yuanchang read the letter and immediately stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanchang read the letter and immediately stopped.

sentences.zh: 漸見疏斥，轉荊王友。

translations.literal: Hongzhi gradually fell under disfavor and was transferred to serve as companion to the Prince of Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi gradually fell under disfavor and was transferred to serve as companion to the Prince of Jing.

sentences.zh: 龍朔中卒。

translations.literal: He died during the Longshuo era.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Longshuo era.

sentences.zh: 方慶年十六，起家越王府參軍。

translations.literal: Fangqing at age sixteen began his career as adjutant in the Prince of Yue's household.
translations.idiomatic: Fangqing at age sixteen began his career as adjutant in the Prince of Yue's household.

sentences.zh: 嚐就記室任希古受《史記》、《漢書》。

translations.literal: He once studied the Records of the Grand Historian and the Book of Han under the recorder Ren Xigu.
translations.idiomatic: He once studied the Records of the Grand Historian and the Book of Han under the recorder Ren Xigu.

sentences.zh: 希古遷為太子舍人，方慶隨之卒業。

translations.literal: When Xigu was transferred to serve as attendant to the crown prince, Fangqing followed him and completed his studies.
translations.idiomatic: When Xigu was transferred to serve as attendant to the crown prince, Fangqing followed him and completed his studies.

sentences.zh: 永淳中，累遷太仆少卿。

translations.literal: During Yongchun he was repeatedly promoted to Vice Minister of the Stud.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongchun he was repeatedly promoted to Vice Minister of the Stud.

sentences.zh: 則天臨朝，拜廣州都督。

translations.literal: When Empress Wu assumed the throne, he was appointed military governor of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu assumed the throne, he was appointed military governor of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 廣州地際南海，每歲有昆侖乘舶以珍物與中國交市。

translations.literal: Guangzhou borders the South Sea; each year Kunlun merchants came by ship with precious goods to trade with China.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzhou borders the South Sea; each year Kunlun merchants came by ship with precious goods to trade with China.

sentences.zh: 舊都督路元睿冒求其貨，昆侖懷刃殺之。

translations.literal: The former governor Lu Yuanrui presumptuously demanded their goods; a Kunlun man, knife hidden, killed him.
translations.idiomatic: The former governor Lu Yuanrui presumptuously demanded their goods; a Kunlun man, knife hidden, killed him.

sentences.zh: 方慶在任數載，秋毫不犯。

translations.literal: Fangqing served several years in office and did not violate so much as an autumn hair.
translations.idiomatic: Fangqing served several years in office and did not violate so much as an autumn hair.

sentences.zh: 又管內諸州首領，舊多貪縱，百姓有詣府稱冤者，府官以先受首領參餉，未嚐鞫問。

translations.literal: Moreover, the tribal chiefs within his jurisdiction had long been greedy and unrestrained; when common people came to the prefecture to plead injustice, prefectural officials, having first received gifts from the chiefs, never investigated.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the tribal chiefs within his jurisdiction had long been greedy and unrestrained; when common people came to the prefecture to plead injustice, prefectural officials, having first received gifts from the chiefs, never investigated.

sentences.zh: 方慶乃集止府僚，絕其交往，首領縱暴者悉繩之，由是境內清肅。

translations.literal: Fangqing then assembled the prefectural staff, cut off their dealings with the chiefs, and punished all chiefs who acted with violence—whereupon the territory became orderly and quiet.
translations.idiomatic: Fangqing then assembled the prefectural staff, cut off their dealings with the chiefs, and punished all chiefs who acted with violence—whereupon the territory became orderly and quiet.

sentences.zh: 當時議者以為有唐以來，治廣州者無出方慶之右。

translations.literal: Contemporaries held that since the founding of Tang, no governor of Guangzhou had surpassed Fangqing.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries held that since the founding of Tang, no governor of Guangzhou had surpassed Fangqing.

sentences.zh: 有制褒之曰：“朕以卿曆職著稱，故授此官，既美化遠聞，實副朝寄。

translations.literal: An edict praised him, saying: "We appoint you to this office because of your distinguished service in successive posts; your fine governance has been heard from afar and truly fulfills the court's trust.
translations.idiomatic: An edict praised him, saying: "We appoint you to this office because of your distinguished service in successive posts; your fine governance has been heard from afar and truly fulfills the court's trust.

sentences.zh: 令賜卿雜采六十段，並瑞錦等物，以彰善政也。”

translations.literal: We now grant you sixty bolts of assorted silks, together with auspicious brocades and other goods, to honor your good governance.
translations.idiomatic: We now grant you sixty bolts of assorted silks, together with auspicious brocades and other goods, to honor your good governance.

sentences.zh: 證聖元年，召拜洛州長史，尋加銀青光祿大夫，封石泉縣男。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengsheng he was summoned and appointed chief secretary of Luozhou; soon he was granted the Silver Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and enfeoffed as Baron of Shiquan County.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhengsheng he was summoned and appointed chief secretary of Luozhou; soon he was granted the Silver Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and enfeoffed as Baron of Shiquan County.

sentences.zh: 萬歲登封元年，轉并州長史，封琅邪縣男。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wansui Dengfeng he was transferred to chief secretary of Bingzhou and enfeoffed as Baron of Langye County.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wansui Dengfeng he was transferred to chief secretary of Bingzhou and enfeoffed as Baron of Langye County.

sentences.zh: 未行，遷鸞台侍郎、同鳳閣鸞台平章事。

translations.literal: Before he departed, he was transferred to Vice Minister of the Hall of the Crane and Associate at the Hall of the Phoenix and Hall of the Crane with the authority of a chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Before he departed, he was transferred to Vice Minister of the Hall of the Crane and Associate at the Hall of the Phoenix and Hall of the Crane with the authority of a chancellor.

sentences.zh: 俄轉鳳閣侍郎，依舊知政事。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Vice Minister of the Hall of the Phoenix, continuing to manage state affairs as before.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to Vice Minister of the Hall of the Phoenix, continuing to manage state affairs as before.

sentences.zh: 神功元年七月，清邊道大總管建安王攸宜破契丹凱還，欲以是月詣闕獻俘。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Shengong, Prince Jian'an Youyi, Grand Commander of the Qingbian Circuit, returned in triumph after defeating the Khitan and wished that month to come to court and present captives.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the first year of Shengong, Prince Jian'an Youyi, Grand Commander of the Qingbian Circuit, returned in triumph after defeating the Khitan and wished that month to come to court and present captives.

sentences.zh: 內史王及善以為將軍入城，例有軍樂，既今上孝明高皇帝忌月，請備而不奏。

translations.literal: Director of the Secretariat Wang Jishan held that when a general enters the city, military music is customary by precedent; since it was the mourning month for the late Emperor Xiaoming Gaozu, he requested that the music be prepared but not performed.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Secretariat Wang Jishan held that when a general enters the city, military music is customary by precedent; since it was the mourning month for the late Emperor Xiaoming Gaozu, he requested that the music be prepared but not performed.

sentences.zh: 方慶奏曰：“臣按禮經，但有忌日，而無忌月。

translations.literal: Fangqing memorialized, saying: "Your subject finds in the ritual classics only mourning days, not mourning months.
translations.idiomatic: Fangqing memorialized, saying: "Your subject finds in the ritual classics only mourning days, not mourning months.

sentences.zh: 晉穆帝納後，用九月九日，是康帝忌月，於時持疑不定。

translations.literal: When Emperor Mu of Jin took an empress, the date chosen was the ninth day of the ninth month—the mourning month of Emperor Kang—and at the time opinion was divided and unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Mu of Jin took an empress, the date chosen was the ninth day of the ninth month—the mourning month of Emperor Kang—and at the time opinion was divided and unsettled.

sentences.zh: 下太常，禮官荀訥議稱：‘禮隻有忌日，無忌月。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; the ritual official Xun Ne argued: 'The rites provide only mourning days, not mourning months.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was referred to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; the ritual official Xun Ne argued: 'The rites provide only mourning days, not mourning months.

sentences.zh: 若有忌月，即有忌時、忌歲，益無理據。

translations.literal: If there were mourning months, there would also be mourning seasons and mourning years—still less reasonable.
translations.idiomatic: If there were mourning months, there would also be mourning seasons and mourning years—still less reasonable.

sentences.zh: ’當時從訥所議。

translations.literal: ' At the time Ne's opinion was followed.
translations.idiomatic: ' At the time Ne's opinion was followed.

sentences.zh: 軍樂是軍容，與常不等，臣謂振作於事無嫌。”

translations.literal: Military music is military display and not the same as ordinary practice; your subject holds that performing it would be without impropriety."
translations.idiomatic: Military music is military display and not the same as ordinary practice; your subject holds that performing it would be without impropriety."

sentences.zh: 則天從之。

translations.literal: Empress Wu followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu followed this.

sentences.zh: 則天嚐幸萬安山玉泉寺，以山逕危懸，欲禦腰輿而上。

translations.literal: Empress Wu once visited the Yuquan Temple on Mount Wan'an; because the mountain path was perilously steep, she wished to ride a waist-litter up.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu once visited the Yuquan Temple on Mount Wan'an; because the mountain path was perilously steep, she wished to ride a waist-litter up.

sentences.zh: 方慶諫曰：“昔漢元帝嚐祭廟，出便門，禦樓船，光祿勳張猛奏曰：‘乘船危，就橋安。

translations.literal: Fangqing remonstrated, saying: "Formerly Emperor Yuan of Han once performed temple sacrifice, went out by the Convenience Gate, and boarded a tower ship; Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Zhang Meng memorialized: 'Going by boat is perilous; taking the bridge is safe.
translations.idiomatic: Fangqing remonstrated, saying: "Formerly Emperor Yuan of Han once performed temple sacrifice, went out by the Convenience Gate, and boarded a tower ship; Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Zhang Meng memorialized: 'Going by boat is perilous; taking the bridge is safe.

sentences.zh: ’元帝乃從橋，即前代舊事。

translations.literal: ' Emperor Yuan then took the bridge—an old precedent from former ages.
translations.idiomatic: ' Emperor Yuan then took the bridge—an old precedent from former ages.

sentences.zh: 今山徑危險，石路曲狹，上瞻駭目，下視寒心，比於樓船，安危不等。

translations.literal: Now the mountain path is perilous, the stone road winding and narrow—looking up startles the eye, looking down chills the heart; compared with a tower ship, safety and danger are not equal.
translations.idiomatic: Now the mountain path is perilous, the stone road winding and narrow—looking up startles the eye, looking down chills the heart; compared with a tower ship, safety and danger are not equal.

sentences.zh: 陛下蒸人父母，奈何踐此畏塗？

translations.literal: Your Majesty is parent to the teeming people—how can you tread this fearful path?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is parent to the teeming people—how can you tread this fearful path?

sentences.zh: 伏望停輿駐蹕。”

translations.literal: Humbly I hope Your Majesty will halt the carriage and pause your progress."
translations.idiomatic: Humbly I hope Your Majesty will halt the carriage and pause your progress."

sentences.zh: 則天納其言而止。

translations.literal: Empress Wu accepted his words and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu accepted his words and stopped.

sentences.zh: 是歲，改封石泉子。

translations.literal: That year his enfeoffment was changed to Viscount of Shiquan.
translations.idiomatic: That year his enfeoffment was changed to Viscount of Shiquan.

sentences.zh: 時有制，每月一日於明堂行告朔之禮。

translations.literal: At the time there was a regulation that on the first day of each month the announcement of the new moon rite was performed at the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: At the time there was a regulation that on the first day of each month the announcement of the new moon rite was performed at the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 司禮博士辟閭仁諝奏議，其略曰：“經史正文，無天子每月告朔之事，唯《禮記·玉藻》云：‘天子聽朔於南門之外。

translations.literal: Doctor of Rites Pilu Renxu submitted a memorial of deliberation, in summary saying: "The canonical texts of the classics and histories contain no account of the Son of Heaven performing monthly new-moon announcements; only the Record of Rites, "Jade Ornaments," says: 'The Son of Heaven receives the new moon outside the southern gate.
translations.idiomatic: Doctor of Rites Pilu Renxu submitted a memorial of deliberation, in summary saying: "The canonical texts of the classics and histories contain no account of the Son of Heaven performing monthly new-moon announcements; only the Record of Rites, "Jade Ornaments," says: 'The Son of Heaven receives the new moon outside the southern gate.

sentences.zh: ’其每月告朔者，諸侯之禮也。

translations.literal: ' Monthly new-moon announcements are the rite of feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: ' Monthly new-moon announcements are the rite of feudal lords.

sentences.zh: 臣謹按《禮論》及《三禮義宗》、《江都集禮》、《貞觀禮》、《顯慶禮》及《祠令》，無天子每月告朔之事。

translations.literal: Your subject respectfully finds in the Treatise on Rites, the Three Rites Meaning Collection, the Jiangdu Collected Rites, the Zhenguan Rites, the Xianqing Rites, and the Sacrificial Statutes no account of the Son of Heaven performing monthly new-moon announcements.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject respectfully finds in the Treatise on Rites, the Three Rites Meaning Collection, the Jiangdu Collected Rites, the Zhenguan Rites, the Xianqing Rites, and the Sacrificial Statutes no account of the Son of Heaven performing monthly new-moon announcements.

sentences.zh: 若以為無明堂故無告朔之禮，有明堂即合告朔，則周、秦有明堂而無天子每月告朔之事。

translations.literal: If one holds that because there was no Bright Hall there was no new-moon announcement rite, and that with a Bright Hall one ought to announce the new moon, then Zhou and Qin had Bright Halls yet no account of the Son of Heaven performing monthly new-moon announcements.
translations.idiomatic: If one holds that because there was no Bright Hall there was no new-moon announcement rite, and that with a Bright Hall one ought to announce the new moon, then Zhou and Qin had Bright Halls yet no account of the Son of Heaven performing monthly new-moon announcements.

sentences.zh: 臣等參求，既無其禮，不可習非，以天子之尊而用諸侯之禮。”

translations.literal: We have jointly investigated and find no such rite; one cannot practice what is wrong and, in the exalted person of the Son of Heaven, employ the rites of feudal lords."
translations.idiomatic: We have jointly investigated and find no such rite; one cannot practice what is wrong and, in the exalted person of the Son of Heaven, employ the rites of feudal lords."

sentences.zh: 方慶又奏議，其略曰：“明堂，天子布政之宮也。

translations.literal: Fangqing also submitted a memorial of deliberation, in summary saying: "The Bright Hall is the palace where the Son of Heaven promulgates government.
translations.idiomatic: Fangqing also submitted a memorial of deliberation, in summary saying: "The Bright Hall is the palace where the Son of Heaven promulgates government.

sentences.zh: 謹按《穀梁傳》云：‘閏者，附月之餘日，天子不以告朔。

translations.literal: Respectfully I find in the Guliang Commentary: 'An intercalary month consists of the surplus days attached to a month; the Son of Heaven does not announce the new moon for it.
translations.idiomatic: Respectfully I find in the Guliang Commentary: 'An intercalary month consists of the surplus days attached to a month; the Son of Heaven does not announce the new moon for it.

sentences.zh: ’‘非禮也。

translations.literal: '' 'It is not according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: '' 'It is not according to ritual.

sentences.zh: 閏以正時，時以作事，事以厚生，生人之道，於是乎在矣。

translations.literal: The intercalary month corrects the seasons; seasons govern affairs; affairs enrich life; the way of sustaining the living lies herein.
translations.idiomatic: The intercalary month corrects the seasons; seasons govern affairs; affairs enrich life; the way of sustaining the living lies herein.

sentences.zh: 不告閏朔，棄時政也。

translations.literal: Not announcing the intercalary new moon abandons governance of the seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Not announcing the intercalary new moon abandons governance of the seasons.

sentences.zh: ’臣據此文，則天子閏月亦告朔矣。

translations.literal: ' According to this passage, the Son of Heaven also announces the new moon in an intercalary month.
translations.idiomatic: ' According to this passage, the Son of Heaven also announces the new moon in an intercalary month.

sentences.zh: 寧有他月而廢其禮乎？

translations.literal: How could other months abolish this rite?
translations.idiomatic: How could other months abolish this rite?

sentences.zh: 先儒舊說，天子行事，一年十八度入明堂矣。

translations.literal: The old teaching of former scholars holds that in the Son of Heaven's conduct he enters the Bright Hall eighteen times a year.
translations.idiomatic: The old teaching of former scholars holds that in the Son of Heaven's conduct he enters the Bright Hall eighteen times a year.

sentences.zh: 大享不問卜，一入也；

translations.literal: The great offering without divination—one entry;
translations.idiomatic: The great offering without divination—one entry;

sentences.zh: 每月告朔，十二入也；

translations.literal: monthly new-moon announcements—twelve entries;
translations.idiomatic: monthly new-moon announcements—twelve entries;

sentences.zh: 四時迎氣，四入也；

translations.literal: welcoming the qi of the four seasons—four entries;
translations.idiomatic: welcoming the qi of the four seasons—four entries;

sentences.zh: 巡狩之年，一入也。

translations.literal: in years of the imperial tour—one entry.
translations.idiomatic: in years of the imperial tour—one entry.

sentences.zh: 今禮官議唯歲首一入耳，與先儒既異，在臣不敢同。

translations.literal: Now the ritual officials argue for only one entry at the year's beginning—already differing from former scholars; your subject dares not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Now the ritual officials argue for only one entry at the year's beginning—already differing from former scholars; your subject dares not agree.

sentences.zh: 宋朝何承天纂集其文，以為《禮論》，雖加編次，事則闕如。

translations.literal: He Chengtian of the Song dynasty compiled the texts into the Treatise on Rites; though he added arrangement, the matter remains deficient.
translations.idiomatic: He Chengtian of the Song dynasty compiled the texts into the Treatise on Rites; though he added arrangement, the matter remains deficient.

sentences.zh: 梁代崔靈恩撰《三禮義宗》，但捃摭前儒，因循故事而已。

translations.literal: Cui Ling'en of the Liang dynasty compiled the Three Rites Meaning Collection, merely gathering former scholars and following old precedents.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Ling'en of the Liang dynasty compiled the Three Rites Meaning Collection, merely gathering former scholars and following old precedents.

sentences.zh: 隋煬帝命學士撰《江都集禮》，隻抄撮舊禮，更無異文。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang of Sui ordered scholars to compile the Jiangdu Collected Rites, simply excerpting old rites with no differing text.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang of Sui ordered scholars to compile the Jiangdu Collected Rites, simply excerpting old rites with no differing text.

sentences.zh: 《貞觀》、《顯慶禮》及《祠令》不言告朔者，蓋為曆代不傳，所以其文乃闕。

translations.literal: The Zhenguan Rites, Xianqing Rites, and Sacrificial Statutes do not mention new-moon announcements—presumably because the practice was not transmitted through successive dynasties, and so the text is lacking.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhenguan Rites, Xianqing Rites, and Sacrificial Statutes do not mention new-moon announcements—presumably because the practice was not transmitted through successive dynasties, and so the text is lacking.

sentences.zh: 各有緣由，不足依據。

translations.literal: Each has its reasons and is insufficient as basis.
translations.idiomatic: Each has its reasons and is insufficient as basis.

sentences.zh: 今禮官引為明證，在臣誠實有疑。”

translations.literal: That the ritual officials now cite these as clear proof—in your subject there is genuine doubt."
translations.idiomatic: That the ritual officials now cite these as clear proof—in your subject there is genuine doubt."

sentences.zh: 則天又令春官廣集眾儒，取方慶、仁諝所奏議，以定得失。

translations.literal: Empress Wu then ordered the Ministry of Rites broadly to assemble the scholars, taking the memorials of deliberation submitted by Fangqing and Renxu to determine what was right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu then ordered the Ministry of Rites broadly to assemble the scholars, taking the memorials of deliberation submitted by Fangqing and Renxu to determine what was right and wrong.

sentences.zh: 時成均博士吳揚善、太學博士郭山惲等奏：“按《周禮》及《三傳》，皆有天子告朔之禮，秦滅《詩》、《書》，由是告朔禮廢。

translations.literal: At the time Director of the Imperial Academy Wu Yangshan, Director of the National University Guo Shanyun, and others memorialized: "According to the Rites of Zhou and the Three Commentaries, all contain the Son of Heaven's new-moon announcement rite; Qin destroyed the Odes and Documents, and thereby the new-moon announcement rite fell into disuse.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Director of the Imperial Academy Wu Yangshan, Director of the National University Guo Shanyun, and others memorialized: "According to the Rites of Zhou and the Three Commentaries, all contain the Son of Heaven's new-moon announcement rite; Qin destroyed the Odes and Documents, and thereby the new-moon announcement rite fell into disuse.

sentences.zh: 望依方慶議。”

translations.literal: We hope to follow Fangqing's deliberation."
translations.idiomatic: We hope to follow Fangqing's deliberation."

sentences.zh: 有制從之。

translations.literal: An edict followed this.
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed this.

sentences.zh: 則天以方慶家多書籍，嚐訪求右軍遺跡。

translations.literal: Empress Wu, because Fangqing's family possessed many books, once sought traces of the Right General's calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu, because Fangqing's family possessed many books, once sought traces of the Right General's calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 方慶奏曰：“臣十代從伯祖羲之書，先有四十餘紙，貞觀十二年，太宗購求，先臣並已進之。

translations.literal: Fangqing memorialized, saying: "Your subject's tenth-generation collateral great-uncle Xizhi's writings originally numbered more than forty sheets; in the twelfth year of Zhenguan Emperor Taizong sought to purchase them, and my forebears all presented them.
translations.idiomatic: Fangqing memorialized, saying: "Your subject's tenth-generation collateral great-uncle Xizhi's writings originally numbered more than forty sheets; in the twelfth year of Zhenguan Emperor Taizong sought to purchase them, and my forebears all presented them.

sentences.zh: 唯有一卷見今在。

translations.literal: Only one scroll remains extant today.
translations.idiomatic: Only one scroll remains extant today.

sentences.zh: 又進臣十一代祖導、十代祖洽、九代祖珣、八代祖曇首、七代祖僧綽、六代祖仲寶、五代祖騫、高祖規、曾祖褒，並九代三從伯祖晉中書令獻之已下二十八人書，共十卷。”

translations.literal: He further presented writings of your subject's eleventh-generation ancestor Dao, tenth-generation ancestor Qia, ninth-generation ancestor Xun, eighth-generation ancestor Tan Shou, seventh-generation ancestor Seng Chuo, sixth-generation ancestor Zhongbao, fifth-generation ancestor Qian, great-grandfather Gui, and great-great-grandfather Bao, together with twenty-eight persons from the ninth-generation third-cousin, Jin Secretariat Director Xianzhi, downward—altogether ten scrolls."
translations.idiomatic: He further presented writings of your subject's eleventh-generation ancestor Dao, tenth-generation ancestor Qia, ninth-generation ancestor Xun, eighth-generation ancestor Tan Shou, seventh-generation ancestor Seng Chuo, sixth-generation ancestor Zhongbao, fifth-generation ancestor Qian, great-grandfather Gui, and great-great-grandfather Bao, together with twenty-eight persons from the ninth-generation third-cousin, Jin Secretariat Director Xianzhi, downward—altogether ten scrolls."

sentences.zh: 則天禦武成殿示群臣，仍令中書舍人崔融為《寶章集》，以敘其事，復賜方慶，當時甚以為榮。

translations.literal: Empress Wu ascended the Wucheng Hall to show the ministers, and ordered Secretariat drafter Cui Rong to compose the Precious Writings Collection to narrate the affair; she again bestowed it on Fangqing—a great honor at the time.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu ascended the Wucheng Hall to show the ministers, and ordered Secretariat drafter Cui Rong to compose the Precious Writings Collection to narrate the affair; she again bestowed it on Fangqing—a great honor at the time.

sentences.zh: 方慶又舉：“令杖‘期喪、大功未葬，不預朝賀；

translations.literal: Fangqing also proposed: "The statute provides: 'During first- and second-degree mourning before burial, one does not participate in court congratulations;
translations.idiomatic: Fangqing also proposed: "The statute provides: 'During first- and second-degree mourning before burial, one does not participate in court congratulations;

sentences.zh: 未終喪，不預宴會。

translations.literal: before mourning is complete, one does not participate in banquets.
translations.idiomatic: before mourning is complete, one does not participate in banquets.

sentences.zh: ’比來朝官不遵禮法，身有哀容，陪預朝會，手舞足蹈，公違憲章，名教既虧，實玷皇化。

translations.literal: ' Recently court officials have not observed ritual law—bearing mourning countenance yet attending court sessions, clapping hands and stamping feet in public violation of statutes; name and teaching are already impaired and truly stain imperial transformation.
translations.idiomatic: ' Recently court officials have not observed ritual law—bearing mourning countenance yet attending court sessions, clapping hands and stamping feet in public violation of statutes; name and teaching are already impaired and truly stain imperial transformation.

sentences.zh: 伏望申明令式，更禁斷。”

translations.literal: Humbly I hope the statutes and regulations may be clarified and further forbidden."
translations.idiomatic: Humbly I hope the statutes and regulations may be clarified and further forbidden."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: This was approved.

sentences.zh: 方慶漸以老疾，乞從閑逸，乃授麟台監修國史。

translations.literal: Fangqing gradually, owing to age and illness, requested leisure and ease; he was then appointed Director of the Forest Terrace to compile the national history.
translations.idiomatic: Fangqing gradually, owing to age and illness, requested leisure and ease; he was then appointed Director of the Forest Terrace to compile the national history.

sentences.zh: 及中宗立為東宮，方慶兼檢校太子左庶子。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong was established as Eastern Palace heir, Fangqing was additionally appointed Acting Left Subordinate of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongzong was established as Eastern Palace heir, Fangqing was additionally appointed Acting Left Subordinate of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 聖曆二年一日，則天欲季冬講武，有司稽緩，延入孟春。

translations.literal: On one day in the second year of Shenli, Empress Wu wished to conduct military exercises in late winter; the responsible officials were slow in preparation and postponed it into early spring.
translations.idiomatic: On one day in the second year of Shenli, Empress Wu wished to conduct military exercises in late winter; the responsible officials were slow in preparation and postponed it into early spring.

sentences.zh: 方慶上疏曰：“謹按《禮記月令》：‘孟冬之月，天子命將帥講武，習射禦角力。

translations.literal: Fangqing submitted a memorial, saying: "Respectfully I find in the Monthly Ordinances of the Record of Rites: 'In the month of early winter, the Son of Heaven orders generals and commanders to conduct military exercises, practicing archery and wrestling.
translations.idiomatic: Fangqing submitted a memorial, saying: "Respectfully I find in the Monthly Ordinances of the Record of Rites: 'In the month of early winter, the Son of Heaven orders generals and commanders to conduct military exercises, practicing archery and wrestling.

sentences.zh: ’此乃三時務農，一時講武，以習射禦，角校才力，蓋王者常事，安不忘危之道也。

translations.literal: ' This is three seasons devoted to agriculture and one season to military exercises—to practice archery and defense, test strength in wrestling; it is the king's regular affair, the way of security without forgetting peril.
translations.idiomatic: ' This is three seasons devoted to agriculture and one season to military exercises—to practice archery and defense, test strength in wrestling; it is the king's regular affair, the way of security without forgetting peril.

sentences.zh: ‘孟春之月，不可以稱兵。

translations.literal: 'In the month of early spring, one may not raise arms.
translations.idiomatic: 'In the month of early spring, one may not raise arms.

sentences.zh: ’兵者，甲胄干戈之總名。

translations.literal: ' Arms are the general name for armor, helmets, shields, and halberds.
translations.idiomatic: ' Arms are the general name for armor, helmets, shields, and halberds.

sentences.zh: 兵金性，克木，春盛德在木，而舉金以害盛德，逆生氣。

translations.literal: Arms belong to the nature of metal, which overcomes wood; in spring the supreme virtue resides in wood—yet to raise metal and harm the supreme virtue reverses the generative qi.
translations.idiomatic: Arms belong to the nature of metal, which overcomes wood; in spring the supreme virtue resides in wood—yet to raise metal and harm the supreme virtue reverses the generative qi.

sentences.zh: ‘孟春行冬令，則水潦為敗，雪霜大摯，首種不入。

translations.literal: 'If in early spring one executes winter ordinances, then floods become ruinous, frost and snow severe, and the first sowing does not take.
translations.idiomatic: 'If in early spring one executes winter ordinances, then floods become ruinous, frost and snow severe, and the first sowing does not take.

sentences.zh: ’蔡邕《月令章句》云：‘太陰新休，少陽尚微，而行冬令以導水氣，故水潦至而敗生物也。

translations.literal: ' Cai Yong's Monthly Ordinances Commentary says: 'Great yin has just rested, lesser yang is still slight—yet to execute winter ordinances and channel water qi causes floods to arrive and ruin living things.
translations.idiomatic: ' Cai Yong's Monthly Ordinances Commentary says: 'Great yin has just rested, lesser yang is still slight—yet to execute winter ordinances and channel water qi causes floods to arrive and ruin living things.

sentences.zh: 雪霜大摯，折陽者也。

translations.literal: Severe frost and snow break the yang.
translations.idiomatic: Severe frost and snow break the yang.

sentences.zh: 太陰幹時，雨雪而霜，故大傷首種。

translations.literal: Great yin overpowers the season; rain, snow, and frost follow—thereby greatly harming the first sowing.
translations.idiomatic: Great yin overpowers the season; rain, snow, and frost follow—thereby greatly harming the first sowing.

sentences.zh: 首種，謂宿麥也，麥以秋種，故謂之首種。

translations.literal: First sowing refers to winter wheat; wheat is sown in autumn, and so is called first sowing.
translations.idiomatic: First sowing refers to winter wheat; wheat is sown in autumn, and so is called first sowing.

sentences.zh: 入，收也，春為沍寒所傷，故至夏麥不成長也。

translations.literal: Not taking refers to not harvesting; spring is harmed by severe cold, and so by summer the wheat does not mature.
translations.idiomatic: Not taking refers to not harvesting; spring is harmed by severe cold, and so by summer the wheat does not mature.

sentences.zh: ’今孟春講武，是行冬令，以陰政犯陽氣，害發生之德。

translations.literal: ' Now to conduct military exercises in early spring is to execute winter ordinances—using yin governance to violate yang qi and harm the virtue of generation.
translations.idiomatic: ' Now to conduct military exercises in early spring is to execute winter ordinances—using yin governance to violate yang qi and harm the virtue of generation.

sentences.zh: 臣恐水潦敗物，霜雪損稼，夏麥不登，無所收入也。

translations.literal: Your subject fears floods will ruin things, frost and snow will damage crops, summer wheat will not ripen, and there will be nothing to harvest.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject fears floods will ruin things, frost and snow will damage crops, summer wheat will not ripen, and there will be nothing to harvest.

sentences.zh: 伏望天恩不違時令，至孟冬教習，以順天道。”

translations.literal: Humbly I hope heavenly grace will not violate the seasons, and that instruction be conducted in early winter to accord with the Way of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Humbly I hope heavenly grace will not violate the seasons, and that instruction be conducted in early winter to accord with the Way of Heaven."

sentences.zh: 手製答曰：“比為久屬太平，多曆年載，人皆廢戰，並悉學文。

translations.literal: An imperial reply in her own hand said: "Recently we have long enjoyed great peace, spanning many years; all have abandoned warfare and devoted themselves entirely to letters.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial reply in her own hand said: "Recently we have long enjoyed great peace, spanning many years; all have abandoned warfare and devoted themselves entirely to letters.

sentences.zh: 今者用整兵威，故令教習。

translations.literal: Now we wish to restore military prestige, and so order instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Now we wish to restore military prestige, and so order instruction.

sentences.zh: 卿以春行冬令，則水潦為敗，舉金傷木，則便害發生。

translations.literal: You hold that executing winter ordinances in spring makes floods ruinous, and raising metal harms wood—thereby harming generation.
translations.idiomatic: You hold that executing winter ordinances in spring makes floods ruinous, and raising metal harms wood—thereby harming generation.

sentences.zh: 循覽所陳，深合典禮，若違此請，乃月令虛行。

translations.literal: Reading through what you have stated, it deeply accords with canonical ritual; if this request were refused, the Monthly Ordinances would be empty in practice.
translations.idiomatic: Reading through what you have stated, it deeply accords with canonical ritual; if this request were refused, the Monthly Ordinances would be empty in practice.

sentences.zh: 佇啟直言，用依來表。”

translations.literal: We await your forthright counsel and will follow your submitted memorial."
translations.idiomatic: We await your forthright counsel and will follow your submitted memorial."

sentences.zh: 是歲，正授太子左庶子，封石泉公，餘並如故，俸料同職事三品，兼侍皇太子讀書。

translations.literal: That year he was formally appointed Left Subordinate of the Heir Apparent, enfeoffed as Duke of Shiquan; the rest remained as before, his salary equal to a third-rank active post, and he additionally attended the crown prince in his studies.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was formally appointed Left Subordinate of the Heir Apparent, enfeoffed as Duke of Shiquan; the rest remained as before, his salary equal to a third-rank active post, and he additionally attended the crown prince in his studies.

sentences.zh: 方慶又上言：“謹按史籍所載，人臣與人主言及上表，未有稱皇太子名者。

translations.literal: Fangqing further submitted: "Respectfully I find in the historical records that when ministers speak with the sovereign or submit memorials, none ever use the crown prince's personal name.
translations.idiomatic: Fangqing further submitted: "Respectfully I find in the historical records that when ministers speak with the sovereign or submit memorials, none ever use the crown prince's personal name.

sentences.zh: 當為太子皇儲，其名尊重，不敢指斥，所以不言。

translations.literal: As the crown prince and imperial heir, his name is revered; one dares not point to it directly, and so does not speak it.
translations.idiomatic: As the crown prince and imperial heir, his name is revered; one dares not point to it directly, and so does not speak it.

sentences.zh: 晉尚書僕射山濤啟事，稱皇太子而不言名。

translations.literal: Shan Tao, Vice Director of the Secretariat under Jin, in his reports referred to the crown prince without speaking his name.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Tao, Vice Director of the Secretariat under Jin, in his reports referred to the crown prince without speaking his name.

sentences.zh: 濤中朝名士，必詳典故，其不稱名，應有憑準。

translations.literal: Tao was a celebrated figure of the central court and surely knew the canonical precedents; that he did not speak the name must have had authoritative basis.
translations.idiomatic: Tao was a celebrated figure of the central court and surely knew the canonical precedents; that he did not speak the name must have had authoritative basis.

sentences.zh: 朝官尚猶如此，宮臣歸則不疑。

translations.literal: If court officials still observe this, palace officials need have no doubt in following it.
translations.idiomatic: If court officials still observe this, palace officials need have no doubt in following it.

sentences.zh: 今東宮殿及門名，皆有觸犯，臨事論啟，回避甚難。

translations.literal: Now the halls and gate names of the Eastern Palace all contain taboo violations; when conducting affairs and submitting reports, avoidance is very difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Now the halls and gate names of the Eastern Palace all contain taboo violations; when conducting affairs and submitting reports, avoidance is very difficult.

sentences.zh: 孝敬皇帝為太子時，改弘教門為崇教門；

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaojing was crown prince, he changed Hongjiao Gate to Chongjiao Gate;
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaojing was crown prince, he changed Hongjiao Gate to Chongjiao Gate;

sentences.zh: 沛王為皇太子，改崇賢館為崇文館。

translations.literal: when the Prince of Pei was crown prince, he changed the Hall of Honoring Worthies to the Hall of Honoring Letters.
translations.idiomatic: when the Prince of Pei was crown prince, he changed the Hall of Honoring Worthies to the Hall of Honoring Letters.

sentences.zh: 皆避名諱，以遵典禮。

translations.literal: All avoided name taboos to observe canonical ritual.
translations.idiomatic: All avoided name taboos to observe canonical ritual.

sentences.zh: 此即成例，足為軌模。

translations.literal: These already constitute precedent, sufficient as models to follow.
translations.idiomatic: These already constitute precedent, sufficient as models to follow.

sentences.zh: 伏望天恩因循舊式，付司改換。”

translations.literal: Humbly I hope heavenly grace will follow the old pattern and charge the responsible offices to make the changes."
translations.idiomatic: Humbly I hope heavenly grace will follow the old pattern and charge the responsible offices to make the changes."

sentences.zh: 製從之。

translations.literal: The edict followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved this.

sentences.zh: 長安二年五月卒，贈袞州都督，諡曰貞。

translations.literal: He died in the fifth month of the second year of Chang'an; posthumously appointed military governor of Yanzhou; posthumous name Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth month of the second year of Chang'an; posthumously appointed military governor of Yanzhou; posthumous name Zhen (Upright).

sentences.zh: 中宗即位，以宮僚之舊，追贈吏部尚書。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong ascended the throne, owing to their old association as palace officials, Fangqing was posthumously granted the title of Minister of the Civil Service.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongzong ascended the throne, owing to their old association as palace officials, Fangqing was posthumously granted the title of Minister of the Civil Service.

sentences.zh: 方慶博學好著述，所撰雜書凡二百餘卷。

translations.literal: Fangqing was broadly learned and fond of writing; miscellaneous works he composed totaled more than two hundred scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Fangqing was broadly learned and fond of writing; miscellaneous works he composed totaled more than two hundred scrolls.

sentences.zh: 尤精《三禮》，好事者多詢訪之。

translations.literal: He was especially expert in the Three Rites; many enthusiasts came to consult him.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially expert in the Three Rites; many enthusiasts came to consult him.

sentences.zh: 每所酬答，鹹有典據，故時人編次，名曰《禮雜答問》。

translations.literal: Each answer he gave had canonical basis; contemporaries compiled them under the title Miscellaneous Questions and Answers on Ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Each answer he gave had canonical basis; contemporaries compiled them under the title Miscellaneous Questions and Answers on Ritual.

sentences.zh: 聚書甚多，不減秘閣，至於圖畫，亦多異本。

translations.literal: He collected many books, not fewer than the Secret Archive; as for paintings, he also had many rare editions.
translations.idiomatic: He collected many books, not fewer than the Secret Archive; as for paintings, he also had many rare editions.

sentences.zh: 諸子莫能守其業，卒後尋亦散亡。

translations.literal: None of his sons could preserve his estate; soon after his death it too was scattered and lost.
translations.idiomatic: None of his sons could preserve his estate; soon after his death it too was scattered and lost.

sentences.zh: 長子光輔，開元中官至潞州刺史。

translations.literal: His eldest son Guangfu, during Kaiyuan, reached the office of prefect of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Guangfu, during Kaiyuan, reached the office of prefect of Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 少子晙，工書知名，尤善琴棋，而性多嚴整，官至殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: His youngest son Jun was renowned for skill in calligraphy, especially adept at zither and chess, yet stern in character; he reached the office of Palace Censor.
translations.idiomatic: His youngest son Jun was renowned for skill in calligraphy, especially adept at zither and chess, yet stern in character; he reached the office of Palace Censor.

sentences.zh: 姚璹，字令璋，散騎常侍思廉之孫也。

translations.literal: Yao Shu, courtesy name Lingzhang, was the grandson of Attendant Cavalier Sili.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shu, courtesy name Lingzhang, was the grandson of Attendant Cavalier Sili.

sentences.zh: 少孤，撫弟妹以友愛稱。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he raised his younger siblings and was known for fraternal affection.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he raised his younger siblings and was known for fraternal affection.

sentences.zh: 博涉經史，有才辯。

translations.literal: Broadly versed in the classics and histories, he had talent for debate.
translations.idiomatic: Broadly versed in the classics and histories, he had talent for debate.

sentences.zh: 永徽中明經擢第。

translations.literal: During Yonghui he passed the Mingjing examination.
translations.idiomatic: During Yonghui he passed the Mingjing examination.

sentences.zh: 累補太子宮門郎。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly appointed gate officer of the crown prince's palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly appointed gate officer of the crown prince's palace.

sentences.zh: 與司議郎孟利貞等奉令撰《瑤山玉彩》書，書成，遷秘書郎。

translations.literal: Together with Reviewer Meng Lizhen and others he was ordered to compile the Jade Splendor of Mount Yao; when the work was complete, he was transferred to secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Reviewer Meng Lizhen and others he was ordered to compile the Jade Splendor of Mount Yao; when the work was complete, he was transferred to secretary.

sentences.zh: 調露中，累遷至中書舍人，封吳興縣男。

translations.literal: During Diaolu he was repeatedly promoted to Secretariat drafter and enfeoffed as Baron of Wuxing County.
translations.idiomatic: During Diaolu he was repeatedly promoted to Secretariat drafter and enfeoffed as Baron of Wuxing County.

sentences.zh: 則天臨朝，遷夏官侍郎。

translations.literal: When Empress Wu assumed the throne, he was transferred to Vice Minister of the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu assumed the throne, he was transferred to Vice Minister of the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 坐從父弟敬節同徐敬業之亂，貶桂州都督府長史。

translations.literal: Because his paternal cousin Jingjie joined Xu Jingye's rebellion, he was demoted to chief secretary of the Guizhou Metropolitan Area Command.
translations.idiomatic: Because his paternal cousin Jingjie joined Xu Jingye's rebellion, he was demoted to chief secretary of the Guizhou Metropolitan Area Command.

sentences.zh: 時則天雅好符瑞，璹至嶺南，訪諸山川草樹，其名號有“武”字者，皆以為上膺國姓，列奏其事。

translations.literal: At the time Empress Wu greatly favored auspicious omens; when Shu reached Lingnan, he investigated mountains, rivers, grasses, and trees, and whatever names contained the character "Wu" he took as Heaven's confirmation of the imperial surname and submitted memorials listing these matters.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Empress Wu greatly favored auspicious omens; when Shu reached Lingnan, he investigated mountains, rivers, grasses, and trees, and whatever names contained the character "Wu" he took as Heaven's confirmation of the imperial surname and submitted memorials listing these matters.

sentences.zh: 則天大悅，召拜天官侍郎。

translations.literal: Empress Wu was greatly pleased and summoned him to serve as Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu was greatly pleased and summoned him to serve as Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 善於選補，時人稱之。

translations.literal: Skilled at selection and appointment, he was praised by contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled at selection and appointment, he was praised by contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 長壽二年，遷文昌左丞、同鳳閣鸞台平章事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Changshou he was transferred to Left Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate at the Hall of the Phoenix and Hall of the Crane with the authority of a chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Changshou he was transferred to Left Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate at the Hall of the Phoenix and Hall of the Crane with the authority of a chancellor.

sentences.zh: 自永徽以後，左、右史雖得對仗承旨，仗下後謀議，皆不預聞。

translations.literal: From Yonghui onward, though Left and Right Historians could receive imperial intent at court, they did not participate in deliberations after the audience ended.
translations.idiomatic: From Yonghui onward, though Left and Right Historians could receive imperial intent at court, they did not participate in deliberations after the audience ended.

sentences.zh: 璹以為帝王謨訓，不可暫無紀述，若不宣自宰相，史官無從得書。

translations.literal: Shu held that the sovereign's counsels and instructions could not for a moment go unrecorded; if not proclaimed by the chancellor, the historiographers would have no means to write them.
translations.idiomatic: Shu held that the sovereign's counsels and instructions could not for a moment go unrecorded; if not proclaimed by the chancellor, the historiographers would have no means to write them.

sentences.zh: 乃表請仗下所言軍國政要，宰相一人專知撰錄，號為時政記，每月封送史館。

translations.literal: He therefore memorialized requesting that military and state affairs spoken after audiences be recorded exclusively by one chancellor, titled Records of Current Governance, sealed and sent monthly to the Historiography Office.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore memorialized requesting that military and state affairs spoken after audiences be recorded exclusively by one chancellor, titled Records of Current Governance, sealed and sent monthly to the Historiography Office.

sentences.zh: 宰相之撰時政記，自璹始也。

translations.literal: The chancellor's compilation of Records of Current Governance began with Shu.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor's compilation of Records of Current Governance began with Shu.

sentences.zh: 是歲九月，坐事轉司賓少卿，罷知政事。

translations.literal: That year in the ninth month, owing to an offense, he was transferred to Vice Minister of Reception and removed from managing state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: That year in the ninth month, owing to an offense, he was transferred to Vice Minister of Reception and removed from managing state affairs.

sentences.zh: 延載初，擢拜納言。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yanzai he was promoted to Chief Censor.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yanzai he was promoted to Chief Censor.

sentences.zh: 有司以璹從父弟犯法，奏言不合更為侍臣。

translations.literal: The responsible offices, because Shu's paternal cousin had violated the law, memorialized that he was unfit to serve again as a palace minister.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices, because Shu's paternal cousin had violated the law, memorialized that he was unfit to serve again as a palace minister.

sentences.zh: 璹上言：“昔王敦稱兵犯順，王導仍典樞機；

translations.literal: Shu submitted: "Formerly Wang Dun raised troops in rebellion, yet Wang Dao still held the keys of state;
translations.idiomatic: Shu submitted: "Formerly Wang Dun raised troops in rebellion, yet Wang Dao still held the keys of state;

sentences.zh: 嵇康戮於晉朝，嵇紹忠於晉室。

translations.literal: Ji Kang was executed under the Jin, yet Ji Shao remained loyal to the Jin house.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Kang was executed under the Jin, yet Ji Shao remained loyal to the Jin house.

sentences.zh: 竊惟前古，尚不為疑；

translations.literal: Reflecting on former ages, this was not held in doubt;
translations.idiomatic: Reflecting on former ages, this was not held in doubt;

sentences.zh: 今奉聖恩，豈由臣下。

translations.literal: now receiving sacred grace—how could this be decided by subordinates?
translations.idiomatic: now receiving sacred grace—how could this be decided by subordinates?

sentences.zh: 必以體例有乖，伏請甘從屏退。”

translations.literal: If protocol truly conflicts, I humbly request to accept dismissal willingly."
translations.idiomatic: If protocol truly conflicts, I humbly request to accept dismissal willingly."

sentences.zh: 則天曰：“此乃我意，卿復何言！

translations.literal: Empress Wu said: "This is my intent—what more have you to say!
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu said: "This is my intent—what more have you to say!

sentences.zh: 但當盡忠，無聽浮說。”

translations.literal: Only devote yourself fully; pay no heed to idle talk.
translations.idiomatic: Only devote yourself fully; pay no heed to idle talk.

sentences.zh: 時武三思率蕃夷酋長，請造天樞於端門外，刻字紀功，以頌周德，璹為督作使。

translations.literal: At the time Wu Sansi led tribal chieftains in requesting that a Celestial Axis be erected outside the Duan Gate, with characters carved to record achievements and praise Zhou virtue; Shu served as superintendent of construction.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Wu Sansi led tribal chieftains in requesting that a Celestial Axis be erected outside the Duan Gate, with characters carved to record achievements and praise Zhou virtue; Shu served as superintendent of construction.

sentences.zh: 證聖初，璹加秋官尚書、同平章事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengsheng, Shu was additionally appointed Minister of Justice with the authority of a chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhengsheng, Shu was additionally appointed Minister of Justice with the authority of a chancellor.

sentences.zh: 是歲，明堂災，則天欲責躬避正殿，璹奏曰：“此實人火，非曰天災。

translations.literal: That year the Bright Hall burned; Empress Wu wished to blame herself and avoid the main hall. Shu memorialized: "This was truly human fire, not what is called a heavenly disaster.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Bright Hall burned; Empress Wu wished to blame herself and avoid the main hall. Shu memorialized: "This was truly human fire, not what is called a heavenly disaster.

sentences.zh: 至如成周宣榭，卜代愈隆；

translations.literal: Consider the Xuan Pavilion of the Cheng-Zhou period—divination showed the dynasty would grow ever more glorious;
translations.idiomatic: Consider the Xuan Pavilion of the Cheng-Zhou period—divination showed the dynasty would grow ever more glorious;

sentences.zh: 漢武建章，盛德彌永。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Han's Jianzhang Palace—its splendid virtue endured ever longer.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Han's Jianzhang Palace—its splendid virtue endured ever longer.

sentences.zh: 臣又見《彌勒下生經》雲，當彌勒成佛之時，七寶台須臾散壞。

translations.literal: Your subject also finds in the Sutra of Maitreya's Descent that when Maitreya attains buddhahood, the seven-jewel platform is swiftly scattered and destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject also finds in the Sutra of Maitreya's Descent that when Maitreya attains buddhahood, the seven-jewel platform is swiftly scattered and destroyed.

sentences.zh: 睹此無常之相，便成正覺之因。

translations.literal: Seeing this mark of impermanence becomes the cause of perfect enlightenment.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing this mark of impermanence becomes the cause of perfect enlightenment.

sentences.zh: 故知聖人之道，隨緣示化，方便之利，博濟良多。

translations.literal: Thus one knows the way of the sage manifests transformation according to conditions; the benefit of skillful means broadly saves many.
translations.idiomatic: Thus one knows the way of the sage manifests transformation according to conditions; the benefit of skillful means broadly saves many.

sentences.zh: 可使由之，義存於此。

translations.literal: One may be guided by this—the principle resides herein.
translations.idiomatic: One may be guided by this—the principle resides herein.

sentences.zh: 況今明堂，乃是布政之所，非宗廟之地，陛下若避正殿，於禮未為得也。”
