translations.literal: Moreover, the Bright Hall today is the place where government is promulgated, not the site of the ancestral temple—if Your Majesty avoids the main hall, ritual is not properly observed."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Bright Hall today is the place where government is promulgated, not the site of the ancestral temple—if Your Majesty avoids the main hall, ritual is not properly observed."

sentences.zh: 左拾遺劉承慶廷奏云：“明堂宗祀之所，今既被焚，陛下宜輟朝思過。”

translations.literal: Left Reminder Liu Chengqing memorialized at court: "The Bright Hall is the place of ancestral sacrifice; now that it has burned, Your Majesty should suspend court and reflect on faults."
translations.idiomatic: Left Reminder Liu Chengqing memorialized at court: "The Bright Hall is the place of ancestral sacrifice; now that it has burned, Your Majesty should suspend court and reflect on faults."

sentences.zh: 璹又持前議以爭之，則天乃依璹奏。

translations.literal: Shu again upheld his earlier deliberation in dispute; Empress Wu then followed Shu's memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Shu again upheld his earlier deliberation in dispute; Empress Wu then followed Shu's memorial.

sentences.zh: 先令璹監造天樞，至是以功當賜爵一等。

translations.literal: Earlier Shu had been ordered to supervise construction of the Celestial Axis; now for this achievement he was due one rank of ennoblement.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Shu had been ordered to supervise construction of the Celestial Axis; now for this achievement he was due one rank of ennoblement.

sentences.zh: 璹表請回贈父一官，乃追贈其父豫州司戶參軍處平為博州刺史。

translations.literal: Shu memorialized requesting that the ennoblement be redirected to his father; his father Chuping, judicial aide of Yuzhou, was posthumously granted the title of prefect of Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shu memorialized requesting that the ennoblement be redirected to his father; his father Chuping, judicial aide of Yuzhou, was posthumously granted the title of prefect of Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 天後將封嵩嶽，命璹總知撰儀注，並充封禪副使。

translations.literal: When the Empress planned to perform the feng and shan rites on Mount Song, she ordered Shu to oversee the drafting of ritual protocols and serve as deputy commissioner for the feng and shan.
translations.idiomatic: When the Empress planned to perform the feng and shan rites on Mount Song, she ordered Shu to oversee the drafting of ritual protocols and serve as deputy commissioner for the feng and shan.

sentences.zh: 及重造明堂，又令璹充使督作，以功加銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When the Bright Hall was rebuilt, she again appointed Shu commissioner to supervise construction; for this achievement he was granted the Silver Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: When the Bright Hall was rebuilt, she again appointed Shu commissioner to supervise construction; for this achievement he was granted the Silver Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 時有大石國使請獻獅子，璹上疏諫曰：“獅子猛獸，唯止食肉，遠從碎葉，以至神都，肉既難得，檢為勞費。

translations.literal: At the time an envoy from Tashkent requested to present a lion. Shu submitted a memorial of remonstrance: "The lion is a fierce beast that eats only meat; coming from far Suyab to the Divine Capital, meat is hard to obtain and supervision entails labor and expense.
translations.idiomatic: At the time an envoy from Tashkent requested to present a lion. Shu submitted a memorial of remonstrance: "The lion is a fierce beast that eats only meat; coming from far Suyab to the Divine Capital, meat is hard to obtain and supervision entails labor and expense.

sentences.zh: 陛下以百姓為心，慮一物有失，鷹犬不蓄，漁獵總停。

translations.literal: Your Majesty takes the common people to heart, fearing harm to any living thing—hawks and hounds are not kept, fishing and hunting are entirely stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty takes the common people to heart, fearing harm to any living thing—hawks and hounds are not kept, fishing and hunting are entirely stopped.

sentences.zh: 運不殺以闡大慈，垂好生以敷至德，凡在飛蠢動，莫不感荷仁恩。

translations.literal: Through non-killing you expound great compassion; through cherishing life you spread supreme virtue—all that flies, crawls, or moves none fails to feel and bear your benevolent grace.
translations.idiomatic: Through non-killing you expound great compassion; through cherishing life you spread supreme virtue—all that flies, crawls, or moves none fails to feel and bear your benevolent grace.

sentences.zh: 豈容自菲薄於身，而厚資給於獸，求之至理，必不然乎。”

translations.literal: How could you be sparing toward yourself yet lavish in supplying a beast? Seeking the utmost principle, it surely cannot be so."
translations.idiomatic: How could you be sparing toward yourself yet lavish in supplying a beast? Seeking the utmost principle, it surely cannot be so."

sentences.zh: 疏奏，遽停來使。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the incoming envoy was immediately stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, the incoming envoy was immediately stopped.

sentences.zh: 又九鼎初成，製令黃金千兩塗之。

translations.literal: Also, when the Nine Cauldrons were first completed, an edict ordered them gilded with a thousand taels of gold.
translations.idiomatic: Also, when the Nine Cauldrons were first completed, an edict ordered them gilded with a thousand taels of gold.

sentences.zh: 璹進諫曰：“夫鼎者神器，貴在質樸自然，無假別為浮飾。

translations.literal: Shu submitted remonstrance: "The cauldron is a sacred vessel; what is valued is plain naturalness, with no need for additional ornament.
translations.idiomatic: Shu submitted remonstrance: "The cauldron is a sacred vessel; what is valued is plain naturalness, with no need for additional ornament.

sentences.zh: 臣觀其狀，先有五彩輝煥，錯雜其間，豈待金色，方為炫耀？”

translations.literal: Your subject observes their form already has five colors shining brilliantly, interwoven among them—must gold be added before they can dazzle?"
translations.idiomatic: Your subject observes their form already has five colors shining brilliantly, interwoven among them—must gold be added before they can dazzle?"

sentences.zh: 則天又從之。

translations.literal: Empress Wu again followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu again followed this.

sentences.zh: 尋屬契丹犯塞，命梁王武三思為榆關道安撫大使、璹為副使以備之。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the Khitan raided the frontier; Prince of Liang Wu Sansi was appointed Pacification Commissioner of the Yuguang Circuit and Shu deputy commissioner to prepare against them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the Khitan raided the frontier; Prince of Liang Wu Sansi was appointed Pacification Commissioner of the Yuguang Circuit and Shu deputy commissioner to prepare against them.

sentences.zh: 及還，坐事，神功初左授益州大都督府長史。

translations.literal: Upon return, owing to an offense, at the beginning of Shengong he was demoted to chief secretary of the Yizhou Metropolitan Area Command.
translations.idiomatic: Upon return, owing to an offense, at the beginning of Shengong he was demoted to chief secretary of the Yizhou Metropolitan Area Command.

sentences.zh: 蜀中官吏多貪暴，璹屢有發擿，奸無所容。

translations.literal: Officials in Shu were mostly greedy and brutal; Shu repeatedly exposed wrongdoing, leaving no room for the corrupt.
translations.idiomatic: Officials in Shu were mostly greedy and brutal; Shu repeatedly exposed wrongdoing, leaving no room for the corrupt.

sentences.zh: 則天嘉之，降璽書勞之曰：“夫嚴霜之下，識貞鬆之擅奇，疾風之前，知勁草之為貴。

translations.literal: Empress Wu commended him and sent an imperial letter of commendation, saying: "Under severe frost one recognizes the pine's singular steadfastness; before fierce wind one knows the tough grass's worth.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu commended him and sent an imperial letter of commendation, saying: "Under severe frost one recognizes the pine's singular steadfastness; before fierce wind one knows the tough grass's worth.

sentences.zh: 物既有此，人亦宜哉。

translations.literal: If things have this quality, should not people as well?
translations.idiomatic: If things have this quality, should not people as well?

sentences.zh: 卿早荷朝恩，委任斯重。

translations.literal: You early received court grace and were entrusted with weighty duty.
translations.idiomatic: You early received court grace and were entrusted with weighty duty.

sentences.zh: 居中作相，弘益已多，防邊訓兵，心力俱盡。

translations.literal: Serving at court as chancellor, you have already brought much benefit; guarding the frontier and training troops, heart and strength alike were exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Serving at court as chancellor, you have already brought much benefit; guarding the frontier and training troops, heart and strength alike were exhausted.

sentences.zh: 歲寒無改，終始不渝。

translations.literal: Unchanged in cold years, constant from beginning to end.
translations.idiomatic: Unchanged in cold years, constant from beginning to end.

sentences.zh: 乃眷蜀中，氓俗殷雜，久缺良守，弊於侵漁，政以賄成，人無措足。

translations.literal: Now regarding Shu—the people and customs are numerous and mixed; good governors have long been lacking; harm comes from extortion; government is achieved through bribes; people have nowhere to set foot.
translations.idiomatic: Now regarding Shu—the people and customs are numerous and mixed; good governors have long been lacking; harm comes from extortion; government is achieved through bribes; people have nowhere to set foot.

sentences.zh: 是用命卿出鎮，寄茲存養。

translations.literal: Therefore we charge you to go out and govern, entrusting you with preserving and nurturing the people.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore we charge you to go out and govern, entrusting you with preserving and nurturing the people.

sentences.zh: 果能攬轡澄清，下車整肅。

translations.literal: You have indeed been able to take the reins and clarify affairs, and upon taking office establish order.
translations.idiomatic: You have indeed been able to take the reins and clarify affairs, and upon taking office establish order.

sentences.zh: 吏不敢犯，奸無所容，前後糾擿，蓋非一緒。

translations.literal: Officials dare not offend; the corrupt find no refuge; expositions before and after amount to more than one thread.
translations.idiomatic: Officials dare not offend; the corrupt find no refuge; expositions before and after amount to more than one thread.

sentences.zh: 貪殘之伍，屏跡於列城；

translations.literal: The greedy and brutal have vanished from the walled cities;
translations.idiomatic: The greedy and brutal have vanished from the walled cities;

sentences.zh: 剽奪之儔，遁形於外境。

translations.literal: plunderers have hidden themselves beyond the borders.
translations.idiomatic: plunderers have hidden themselves beyond the borders.

sentences.zh: 詎勞期月，康此黎元，言念德聲，良深嘉尚。

translations.literal: Need one labor a full month—yet the people are at peace; thinking of your virtuous reputation, we deeply commend and honor it.
translations.idiomatic: In less than a month you have brought peace to the people; thinking of your virtuous reputation, we deeply commend and honor it.

sentences.zh: 宜布琅邪之化，當以豫州為法。”

translations.literal: You should spread the transformation of Langye; take Yuzhou as the model."
translations.idiomatic: You should spread the transformation of Langye; take Yuzhou as the model."

sentences.zh: 則天又嚐謂侍臣曰：“凡為長官，能清自身者甚易，清得僚吏者甚難。

translations.literal: Empress Wu also once told her attending ministers: "For any chief official, keeping oneself clean is very easy; keeping one's subordinate officials clean is very hard.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu also once told her attending ministers: "For any chief official, keeping oneself clean is very easy; keeping one's subordinate officials clean is very hard.

sentences.zh: 至於姚璹，可謂兼之矣。”

translations.literal: As for Yao Shu, one may say he achieved both.
translations.idiomatic: As for Yao Shu, one may say he achieved both.

sentences.zh: 其一曰：臣聞賈誼曰：“選天下之端士，孝悌博聞有道術者，使與太子居處出入。

translations.literal: The first reads: Your subject has heard Jia Yi say: "Select upright scholars from throughout the realm—those filial, fraternal, broadly learned, and possessed of the Way and skill—and have them dwell and go in and out with the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: The first reads: Your subject has heard Jia Yi say: "Select upright scholars from throughout the realm—those filial, fraternal, broadly learned, and possessed of the Way and skill—and have them dwell and go in and out with the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 故太子見正事，聞正言，行正道，左右前後皆正人也。

translations.literal: Thus the crown prince sees upright affairs, hears upright words, and walks the upright path—those to his left and right, before and behind, are all upright men.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the crown prince sees upright affairs, hears upright words, and walks the upright path—those to his left and right, before and behind, are all upright men.

sentences.zh: 夫習與正人居之，不能無正；

translations.literal: One who habitually dwells with upright men cannot fail to become upright;
translations.idiomatic: One who habitually dwells with upright men cannot fail to become upright;

sentences.zh: 習與不正人居之，不能無不正。

translations.literal: one who habitually dwells with un upright men cannot fail to become not upright.
translations.idiomatic: one who habitually dwells with un upright men cannot fail to become not upright.

sentences.zh: 太子既冠成人，免於保傅之嚴，則有記過之史。

translations.literal: When the crown prince has capped his head and reached adulthood, freed from the strictness of tutors and guardians, there are historians who record faults.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince has capped his head and reached adulthood, freed from the strictness of tutors and guardians, there are historians who record faults.

sentences.zh: 徹膳之宰，進善之旌，誹謗之木，敢諫之鼓，瞽史誦箴，大夫進謀，故習與智長，化與心成。

translations.literal: Stewards who withdraw meals, banners that commend goodness, posts for criticism, drums for bold remonstrance, blind historians who recite admonitions, grandees who advance counsel—thus habit grows with wisdom, and transformation completes in the heart.
translations.idiomatic: Stewards who withdraw meals, banners that commend goodness, posts for criticism, drums for bold remonstrance, blind historians who recite admonitions, grandees who advance counsel—thus habit grows with wisdom, and transformation completes in the heart.

sentences.zh: 夫教得而左右正，則太子正矣；

translations.literal: When teaching succeeds and those at his side are upright, then the crown prince is upright;
translations.idiomatic: When teaching succeeds and those at his side are upright, then the crown prince is upright;

sentences.zh: 太子正而天下定矣。”

translations.literal: when the crown prince is upright, the realm is settled."
translations.idiomatic: when the crown prince is upright, the realm is settled."

sentences.zh: 臣又聞之，木從繩則正，後從諫則聖。

translations.literal: Your subject has also heard that wood follows the line and becomes straight; a sovereign follows remonstrance and becomes sage.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject has also heard that wood follows the line and becomes straight; a sovereign follows remonstrance and becomes sage.

sentences.zh: 善言古者，所以驗於今。

translations.literal: Speaking well of antiquity is how one verifies the present.
translations.idiomatic: Speaking well of antiquity is how one verifies the present.

sentences.zh: 伏惟殿下睿德洪深，天姿聰敏，近代成敗，前古安危，莫不懸鑒在心，動合典禮。

translations.literal: Humbly considering that Your Highness's sagely virtue is vast and deep, your heavenly endowment keen and quick—recent success and failure, ancient security and peril—none fails to hang as a mirror in your heart; your actions accord with canonical ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Humbly considering that Your Highness's sagely virtue is vast and deep, your heavenly endowment keen and quick—recent success and failure, ancient security and peril—none fails to hang as a mirror in your heart; your actions accord with canonical ritual.

sentences.zh: 臣以庸朽，濫居輔弼，虛備耳目，叨預股肱，輒薦塵露，庶裨山海。

translations.literal: Your subject, mediocre and decayed, undeservedly occupies the place of assistant; vainly serving as eyes and ears, presumptuously among your arms and legs—I rashly offer dust and dew, hoping it may add a grain to mountains and seas.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject, mediocre and decayed, undeservedly occupies the place of assistant; vainly serving as eyes and ears, presumptuously among your arms and legs—I rashly offer dust and dew, hoping it may add a grain to mountains and seas.

sentences.zh: 伏以內置作坊，工巧得入宮闈之內、禁衛之所，或言語內出，或事狀外通，小人無知，不識輕重，因為詐偽，有玷徽猷。

translations.literal: Humbly considering that workshops are established within the palace, skilled artisans may enter the inner quarters and guarded precincts—words pass outward from within, or affairs connect outside—small men, ignorant and unaware of weight, commit fraud and stain your fine governance.
translations.idiomatic: Humbly considering that workshops are established within the palace, skilled artisans may enter the inner quarters and guarded precincts—words pass outward from within, or affairs connect outside—small men, ignorant and unaware of weight, commit fraud and stain your fine governance.

sentences.zh: 臣望並付所司，以停宮內造作。

translations.literal: Your subject hopes all may be entrusted to the responsible offices to halt construction within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject hopes all may be entrusted to the responsible offices to halt construction within the palace.

sentences.zh: 如或要須役造，猶望宮外安置，庶得工匠不於宮禁出入。

translations.literal: If labor and construction are truly necessary, I still hope they may be placed outside the palace, so that artisans need not enter and leave the forbidden precincts.
translations.idiomatic: If labor and construction are truly necessary, I still hope they may be placed outside the palace, so that artisans need not enter and leave the forbidden precincts.

sentences.zh: 其二曰：臣聞漢文帝身衣弋綈，足履革舄；

translations.literal: The second reads: Your subject has heard that Emperor Wen of Han wore coarse silk and leather shoes on his feet;
translations.idiomatic: The second reads: Your subject has heard that Emperor Wen of Han wore coarse silk and leather shoes on his feet;

sentences.zh: 齊高帝欄檻用銅者，皆易以鐵。

translations.literal: Emperor Gao of Qi replaced all copper used in railings and balustrades with iron.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao of Qi replaced all copper used in railings and balustrades with iron.

sentences.zh: 經侯帶玉具劍環珮以過魏，太子不視，經侯曰：“魏國亦有寶乎？”

translations.literal: Marquis Jing passed through Wei wearing a jade-fitted sword with ring and pendant; the crown prince did not look. Marquis Jing said: "Does the state of Wei also have treasures?"
translations.idiomatic: Marquis Jing passed through Wei wearing a jade-fitted sword with ring and pendant; the crown prince did not look. Marquis Jing said: "Does the state of Wei also have treasures?"

sentences.zh: 太子曰：“主信臣忠，魏之寶也。”

translations.literal: The crown prince said: "When the lord trusts and ministers are loyal—that is Wei's treasure."
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince said: "When the lord trusts and ministers are loyal—that is Wei's treasure."

sentences.zh: 經侯委劍珮而去。

translations.literal: Marquis Jing cast off sword and pendant and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis Jing cast off sword and pendant and departed.

sentences.zh: 太子使追還之，謂曰：“珠玉珍玩，寒不可衣，饑不可食，無遺我賊。”

translations.literal: The crown prince sent men to pursue and return them, saying: "Pearls, jade, and precious curios—cold cannot be clothed with them, hunger cannot be fed by them; leave me no plunderers."
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince sent men to pursue and return them, saying: "Pearls, jade, and precious curios—cold cannot be clothed with them, hunger cannot be fed by them; leave me no plunderers."

sentences.zh: 經侯杜門不出。

translations.literal: Marquis Jing shut his door and did not go out.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis Jing shut his door and did not go out.

sentences.zh: 臣觀聖賢經籍，務以簡素為貴；

translations.literal: Your subject observes that in the scriptures of sages and worthies, simplicity is valued;
translations.idiomatic: Your subject observes that in the scriptures of sages and worthies, simplicity is valued;

sentences.zh: 皇王政化，皆以菲薄為德。

translations.literal: the governance and transformation of emperors and kings all take frugality as virtue.
translations.idiomatic: the governance and transformation of emperors and kings all take frugality as virtue.

sentences.zh: 伏惟殿下留心恭儉，靡尚浮奢。

translations.literal: Humbly considering that Your Highness attends to reverence and frugality and does not esteem empty extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: Humbly considering that Your Highness attends to reverence and frugality and does not esteem empty extravagance.

sentences.zh: 臣愚猶望損之又損之，居簡以行簡，減省造作，節量用度。

translations.literal: Your subject, though foolish, still hopes for reduction upon reduction—dwelling in simplicity to act in simplicity, cutting construction, and moderating expenditure.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject, though foolish, still hopes for reduction upon reduction—dwelling in simplicity to act in simplicity, cutting construction, and moderating expenditure.

sentences.zh: 其三曰：臣聞銀牖銅樓，宮闈嚴秘，門閤來往，皆有簿曆。

translations.literal: The third reads: Your subject has heard that silver windows and copper towers—the inner palace is strictly sealed; all who pass through gates and doors are recorded in ledgers.
translations.idiomatic: The third reads: Your subject has heard that silver windows and copper towers—the inner palace is strictly sealed; all who pass through gates and doors are recorded in ledgers.

sentences.zh: 殿下時有所須，唯門司宣令，或恐奸偽之輩，因此妄為增減，脫有文狀舛錯，事理便即差違。

translations.literal: When Your Highness occasionally requires something, only the gate office proclaims the order—or so one fears that deceitful persons may thereby arbitrarily add or subtract; if documents err, affairs immediately go astray.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Highness occasionally requires something, only the gate office proclaims the order—or so one fears that deceitful persons may thereby arbitrarily add or subtract; if documents err, affairs immediately go astray.

sentences.zh: 且近日呂升之便乃代署宣敕，伏賴殿下睿敏，當即覺其奸偽，自餘臣下庸淺，豈能深辨真虛？

translations.literal: Moreover, recently Lü Shengzhi presumptuously signed and proclaimed edicts in another's place—humbly relying on Your Highness's keen intelligence, you immediately detected the fraud; as for the rest of us shallow subordinates, how could we deeply distinguish truth from falsehood?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, recently Lü Shengzhi presumptuously signed and proclaimed edicts in another's place—humbly relying on Your Highness's keen intelligence, you immediately detected the fraud; as for the rest of us shallow subordinates, how could we deeply distinguish truth from falsehood?

sentences.zh: 望墨令及覆事行下，並用內印印畫署之後，冀得免有詐假，乃是長久規模。

translations.literal: I hope that written orders and submitted replies sent down may all be stamped and signed with the inner seal afterward, so that fraud may be avoided—this would be a lasting model.
translations.idiomatic: I hope that written orders and submitted replies sent down may all be stamped and signed with the inner seal afterward, so that fraud may be avoided—this would be a lasting model.

sentences.zh: 臣又聞之，忠臣事君，有犯而無隱；

translations.literal: Your subject has also heard that loyal ministers serve their lord with offense yet without concealment;
translations.idiomatic: Your subject has also heard that loyal ministers serve their lord with offense yet without concealment;

sentences.zh: 明主馭下，納諫以進德。

translations.literal: enlightened lords govern subordinates and accept remonstrance to advance in virtue.
translations.idiomatic: enlightened lords govern subordinates and accept remonstrance to advance in virtue.

sentences.zh: 故《書》云：“有言逆於誌，必求諸道；

translations.literal: Thus the Documents say: "When words oppose one's intent, one must seek them in the Way;
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Documents say: "When words oppose one's intent, one must seek them in the Way;

sentences.zh: 有言順於心，必求諸非道。”

translations.literal: when words accord with one's heart, one must seek them in what is not the Way."
translations.idiomatic: when words accord with one's heart, one must seek them in what is not the Way."

sentences.zh: 伏惟殿下仁明昭著，聖敬日躋，探幽洞微，窮神索隱。

translations.literal: Humbly considering that Your Highness's benevolence and clarity are manifest, sacred reverence ascends daily, probing the hidden and penetrating the subtle, exhausting spirit to seek the concealed.
translations.idiomatic: Humbly considering that Your Highness's benevolence and clarity are manifest, sacred reverence ascends daily, probing the hidden and penetrating the subtle, exhausting spirit to seek the concealed.

sentences.zh: 事之善惡，毫厘靡差；

translations.literal: The good and evil of affairs—not a hair's breadth of error;
translations.idiomatic: The good and evil of affairs—not a hair's breadth of error;

sentences.zh: 理有危疑，錙銖無爽。

translations.literal: where principle is perilous or doubtful, not a speck of deviation.
translations.idiomatic: where principle is perilous or doubtful, not a speck of deviation.

sentences.zh: 臣以庸謬，叨侍春闈，職居獻替，豈敢緘默！

translations.literal: Your subject, mediocre and mistaken, presumptuously attends the Eastern Palace; duty lies in offering and replacing—how dare I remain silent!
translations.idiomatic: Your subject, mediocre and mistaken, presumptuously attends the Eastern Palace; duty lies in offering and replacing—how dare I remain silent!

sentences.zh: 其四曰：臣聞聖人不專其德，賢智必有所師。

translations.literal: The fourth reads: Your subject has heard that sages do not monopolize virtue; the worthy and wise must have teachers.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth reads: Your subject has heard that sages do not monopolize virtue; the worthy and wise must have teachers.

sentences.zh: 故曰：與善人言，如入芝蘭之室，久自芬芳；

translations.literal: Thus it is said: speaking with good men is like entering a room of orchids and angelica—long exposure makes one fragrant;
translations.idiomatic: Thus it is said: speaking with good men is like entering a room of orchids and angelica—long exposure makes one fragrant;

sentences.zh: 與不善人言，如火銷膏，不覺而盡。

translations.literal: speaking with not good men is like fire melting grease—without noticing, one is consumed.
translations.idiomatic: speaking with not good men is like fire melting grease—without noticing, one is consumed.

sentences.zh: 今司經見無學士，供奉未有侍讀，伏望時因視膳，奏請置人。

translations.literal: Now the Directorate of Classics has no erudite scholars; the palace service has no reading attendant—I humbly hope that when Your Highness views meals, you may memorialize to appoint persons.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Directorate of Classics has no erudite scholars; the palace service has no reading attendant—I humbly hope that when Your Highness views meals, you may memorialize to appoint persons.

sentences.zh: 所冀講席談筵，務盡忠規之道；

translations.literal: What is hoped is that at lecture seats and discussion gatherings, the way of loyal counsel may be fully pursued;
translations.idiomatic: What is hoped is that at lecture seats and discussion gatherings, the way of loyal counsel may be fully pursued;

sentences.zh: 披文擿句，方資審諭之勤。

translations.literal: unfolding texts and selecting passages may then supply the diligence of careful instruction.
translations.idiomatic: unfolding texts and selecting passages may then supply the diligence of careful instruction.

sentences.zh: 臣又聞臣之事主，必盡乃誠；

translations.literal: Your subject has also heard that ministers serving their lord must exhaust their sincerity;
translations.idiomatic: Your subject has also heard that ministers serving their lord must exhaust their sincerity;

sentences.zh: 君之進賢，務求忠讜。

translations.literal: lords advancing the worthy must seek loyal forthrightness.
translations.idiomatic: lords advancing the worthy must seek loyal forthrightness.

sentences.zh: 伏惟殿下養德儲闈，以端靜為務；

translations.literal: Humbly considering that Your Highness cultivates virtue in the heir's quarters and makes upright quietude your task;
translations.idiomatic: Humbly considering that Your Highness cultivates virtue in the heir's quarters and makes upright quietude your task;

sentences.zh: 恭膺守器，以學業為先。

translations.literal: reverently bearing the vessel of succession, you put study first.
translations.idiomatic: reverently bearing the vessel of succession, you put study first.

sentences.zh: 經所以立行修身，史所以諳識成敗。

translations.literal: The classics establish conduct and cultivate the person; histories supply familiarity with success and failure.
translations.idiomatic: The classics establish conduct and cultivate the person; histories supply familiarity with success and failure.

sentences.zh: 雅誥既習，忠孝乃成，傳記方通，安危斯辨。

translations.literal: When elegant decrees are mastered, loyalty and filial piety are achieved; when chronicles are understood, security and peril are distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: When elegant decrees are mastered, loyalty and filial piety are achieved; when chronicles are understood, security and peril are distinguished.

sentences.zh: 知父子君臣之道，識古今鑒戒之規，經史為先，斯乃急務。

translations.literal: Knowing the way of father and son, lord and minister; recognizing the rules of ancient and modern mirrors and warnings—classics and histories first: this is the urgent task.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing the way of father and son, lord and minister; recognizing the rules of ancient and modern mirrors and warnings—classics and histories first: this is the urgent task.

sentences.zh: 至於工巧造作，僚吏直司，實為末事，無足勞慮。

translations.literal: As for craftsmanship and construction, handled by subordinate clerks—these are truly minor matters, not worth troubling over.
translations.idiomatic: As for craftsmanship and construction, handled by subordinate clerks—these are truly minor matters, not worth troubling over.

sentences.zh: 臣以庸淺，獻替是司，臣而不言，負譴聖日，言而獲罪，是所甘心。

translations.literal: Your subject, shallow and mediocre, is charged with offering and replacing—a minister who does not speak bears reproach on a sacred day; to speak and incur punishment is what I accept willingly.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject, shallow and mediocre, is charged with offering and replacing—a minister who does not speak bears reproach on a sacred day; to speak and incur punishment is what I accept willingly.

sentences.zh: 伏願留意經書，簡略細事，一蒙采納，萬殞無辭。

translations.literal: Humbly I wish you would attend to the classics and simplify minor affairs; if but once adopted, though I die ten thousand deaths I would have no complaint.
translations.idiomatic: Humbly I wish you would attend to the classics and simplify minor affairs; if but once adopted, though I die ten thousand deaths I would have no complaint.

sentences.zh: 乞降儲明，俯矜狂瞽。

translations.literal: I beg that stored brilliance descend and look down in pity on my mad blindness.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that stored brilliance descend and look down in pity on my mad blindness.

sentences.zh: 疏奏，太子雖稱善，竟不悛革。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the crown prince praised it but in the end did not reform.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, the crown prince praised it but in the end did not reform.

sentences.zh: 太子敗，詔遣索其宮中，得班諫書，中宗嘉其切直。

translations.literal: When the crown prince fell, an edict was sent to search his palace; Ban's remonstrance was found; Zhongzong commended its blunt directness.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince fell, an edict was sent to search his palace; Ban's remonstrance was found; Zhongzong commended its blunt directness.

sentences.zh: 時宮臣皆貶黜，唯班擢拜右散騎常侍。

translations.literal: At the time all palace officials were demoted; only Ban was promoted to Right Attendant Cavalier.
translations.idiomatic: At the time all palace officials were demoted; only Ban was promoted to Right Attendant Cavalier.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，遷秘書監。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was transferred to Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was transferred to Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 睿宗即位，累授戶部尚書，轉太子賓客。

translations.literal: When Ruizong ascended the throne, Ban was repeatedly granted the title of Minister of Revenue and transferred to Companion of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruizong ascended the throne, Ban was repeatedly granted the title of Minister of Revenue and transferred to Companion of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 先天二年，加金紫光祿大夫，復拜戶部尚書。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xiantian he was granted the Gold Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and again appointed Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xiantian he was granted the Gold Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and again appointed Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 班與兄弟璹，數年間俱為定州刺史、戶部尚書，時人榮之。

translations.literal: Ban and his brother Shu within a few years both served as prefect of Dingzhou and Minister of Revenue; contemporaries regarded this as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: Ban and his brother Shu within a few years both served as prefect of Dingzhou and Minister of Revenue; contemporaries regarded this as an honor.

sentences.zh: 開元二年卒，年七十四。

translations.literal: He died in the second year of Kaiyuan at age seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Kaiyuan at age seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 班嘗以其曾祖察所撰《漢書訓纂》，多爲後之注《漢書》者隱沒名氏，將爲己説；

translations.literal: Ban once found that in the Han Shu Instruction Compilation composed by his great-grandfather Cha, many later commentators on the Book of Han concealed the author's name and took the material as their own exposition;
translations.idiomatic: Ban once found that in the Han Shu Instruction Compilation composed by his great-grandfather Cha, many later commentators on the Book of Han concealed the author's name and took the material as their own exposition;

sentences.zh: 班乃撰《漢書紹訓》四十卷，以發明舊義，行於代。

translations.literal: Ban therefore compiled forty scrolls of the Han Shu Continuation of Instruction to elucidate the old meaning; it circulated in his age.
translations.idiomatic: Ban therefore compiled forty scrolls of the Han Shu Continuation of Instruction to elucidate the old meaning; it circulated in his age.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：天子有諍臣七人，雖無道不失其天下。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: A Son of Heaven has seven remonstrating ministers; though lacking the Way, he does not lose his realm.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer says: A Son of Heaven has seven remonstrating ministers; though lacking the Way, he does not lose his realm.

sentences.zh: 致廬陵復位，唐祚中興，諍由狄公，一人以蔽。

translations.literal: Restoring the Prince of Luling and renewing Tang's fortune—remonstrance came from the Duke of Di; one man suffices to cover the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Restoring the Prince of Luling and renewing Tang's fortune—remonstrance came from the Duke of Di; one man suffices to cover the matter.

sentences.zh: 或曰：許之太甚。

translations.literal: Some say: This praises him too much.
translations.idiomatic: Some say: This praises him too much.

sentences.zh: 答曰：當革命之時，朋邪甚眾，非推誠竭力，致身忘家者，孰能與於此乎！

translations.literal: The reply: At the time of dynastic change, faction and wickedness were many; unless one pushed sincerity to the utmost, gave body and forgot family—who could share in this!
translations.idiomatic: The reply: At the time of dynastic change, faction and wickedness were many; unless one pushed sincerity to the utmost, gave body and forgot family—who could share in this!

sentences.zh: 仁傑流死不避，骨鯁有彰，雖逢好殺無辜，能使終畏大義。

translations.literal: Renjie faced exile and death without shrinking; his unyielding spine was manifest; though he encountered a ruler who loved killing the innocent, he could make her ultimately fear great principle.
translations.idiomatic: Renjie faced exile and death without shrinking; his unyielding spine was manifest; though he encountered a ruler who loved killing the innocent, he could make her ultimately fear great principle.

sentences.zh: 竟存天下，豈不然乎！

translations.literal: In the end he preserved the realm—is it not so!
translations.idiomatic: In the end he preserved the realm—is it not so!

sentences.zh: 王方慶幹城南海，羽冀東宮，台閣樞機，無不功濟，所謂君子不器者也。

translations.literal: Wang Fangqing buttressed the realm in the South Sea, winged the Eastern Palace, and in hall and secretariat alike achieved merit in every task—the so-called gentleman who is not a single vessel.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fangqing buttressed the realm in the South Sea, winged the Eastern Palace, and in hall and secretariat alike achieved merit in every task—the so-called gentleman who is not a single vessel.

sentences.zh: 苟非文學，斯焉取斯。

translations.literal: If not for literary learning, where would such a man be taken from?
translations.idiomatic: If not for literary learning, where would such a man be taken from?

sentences.zh: 璹成都布政，始卒不侔；

translations.literal: Shu governed Chengdu—beginning and end were not alike;
translations.idiomatic: Shu governed Chengdu—beginning and end were not alike;

sentences.zh: 相國上章，或否或中。

translations.literal: as chancellor his memorials were sometimes wrong, sometimes right.
translations.idiomatic: as chancellor his memorials were sometimes wrong, sometimes right.

sentences.zh: 且焚明堂而避正殿，固諍何多；

translations.literal: When the Bright Hall burned and he argued against avoiding the main hall—how much was his firm remonstrance;
translations.idiomatic: When the Bright Hall burned and he argued against avoiding the main hall—how much was his firm remonstrance;

sentences.zh: 黜唐頌而立天樞，一言非措。

translations.literal: yet to dismiss Tang praise and erect the Celestial Axis—one word was wrongly placed.
translations.idiomatic: yet to dismiss Tang praise and erect the Celestial Axis—one word was wrongly placed.

sentences.zh: 矧乃妄求符瑞，已失忠貞；

sentences.zh: 班規諫有才，牧守多善，儲幄之任，可謂得人。
